title: cGMP Facilities
description:
RESPONSIBILITIES:

The cGMP Compliance Handler is typically scheduled on eight hour shifts five days a week. cGMP Compliance Handler must have the flexibility to work on other shifts or overtime when needed. The cGMP Handler must be able to perform job duties with minimal direct supervision and is required to follow an established performance protocol in meeting customary work goals. The position requires a self-started, who can multi-task and adjust to a variety of assignments. The cGMP Compliance Handler must consistently demonstrate effective teamwork behavior. The cGMP Handler will be required to work in several areas of the plant. The cGMP Compliance Handler must have the ability to perform under conditions of continuous physical activity in the execution of their job and lift to 50lbs. As with all employees the cGMP Compliance Handler implements and supports the environmental, health, and safety (EH&S) management system and the company’s EH&S and Quality Policy.

cGMP Facility Compliance Handler will be accountable to the following job duties:

  • cGMP Compliance Handler will sweep debris, wash down walkways, stack pallets, roll up hoses and perform work in non-accessible areas of the plant in compliance with cGMP policies and procedures.
  • Operates forklifts to empty trash dumpsters, and picks up empty drums
  • California Clean
  • Cleaning of storm drains and dikes
  • Labeling of DOT drums
  • Loading of Hazardous Material
  • Pothole Patching
  • Install/ hang signs
  • Rain Gutter Repair and cleaning
  • Window screen repair

California Consumer Privacy Act ("CCPA")

The Company is committed to complying with the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) and all data privacy and laws in the jurisdictions in which it recruits and hires employees. We collect the following categories of personal information for the purpose of hiring the best qualified applicants and to comply with applicable employment laws: Name and contact information; Job preference and work availability; Social Security Number and/or other identification information; Education and qualifications; Employment history and experience; Military service; Reference and background check information, including relevant criminal history and credit history; Social media information; Pre-employment test results; Post-offer medical examination information and results, including drug test results; Voluntary self-disclosure information regarding minority, veteran, and disability status; and Information provided by you during the hiring process.

Tate & Lyle is an equal opportunity employer, committed to the strength of an inclusive workforce.

title: Lead Diagnostic Testing Tech
description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. When we say every member of our community, that includes our employees. We know that when our employees feel cared for, heard and valued, they are inspired to create moments that exceed expectations, while prioritizing safety, compassion, personalization and efficiency. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

Position responsible for fulfilling a leadership role in the non-invasive cardiology department of the facility. Acts as a clinical expert role in the delivery and management of comprehensive patient care within the non-invasive cardiology department, utilizing research and evidence-based practice as necessary. Position is responsible for providing and coordinating expert care to patients from multiple services/specialties, and for complex diagnosis.

Description:

Senior technologist with knowledge of interdepartmental and inter-hospital policies, procedures and departmental guidelines, and demonstrates excellence while carrying out these policies. The Lead Technologist monitors and maintains responsibility for department's high quality patient care by matching patient needs with departmental resources. The Lead Technologist possesses the experience, knowledge, abilities and willingness to act as a clinical resource person. In addition, they provide operations coordination and professional leadership. The Lead Technologist exhibits strong leadership skills, including the willingness and ability to hold department staff accountable for customer relations, risk reduction and process improvement initiatives on a 24 hour basis, and ensuring all quality standards.

Job Description

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Graduate of an accredited School for Medical Professions, required

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified in Basic or Advanced Life Support, required
  • One (1) of the following required:
  • Current State of Texas Nursing License; or
  • Registered Cardiac Sonographer (RCS) by the Cardiovascular Credentialing International; or
  • Registered Congenital Cardiac Sonographer (RCCS) by the Cardiovascular Credentialing International; or
  • Registered Diagnostic Cardiac Sonographer (RDCS) by the American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonographers (ARDMS); or
  • Registered Vascular Sonographer by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT-VS); or
  • Registered Vascular Technologist (RVT) by the American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonographers; or
  • Registered Vascular Specialist (RVS) by Cardiovascular Credentialing International; or
  • Medical Radiologic Technologist Licensed by Texas Medical Board; or
  • Registered Nuclear Medicine Technologist (ARRT-N) by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists; or
  • Certified Nuclear Medicine Technologist (CNMT) by the Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board (NMTCB)

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • Five (5) years of prior diagnostic testing experience
  • Ability to lift and/or maneuver patients in conjunction with others in order to perform job functions

Principal Accountabilities

  • Authorized to plan, coordinate, and direct all activities between diagnostic testing and nursing staff, emergency/critical care and primary physicians, including registration personnel to facilitate rapid patient flow through the department in order to attain positive outcomes.
  • Directs and evaluates departmental throughput; delegates or provides backup assistance.
  • Makes daily assignments for all departmental personnel. Has thorough understanding of care required for all services provided in department, identifies and utilizes available resources to resolve any problems.
  • Ensures safe care to patients and adheres to and develops evidence-based practice procedures, policies, and standards of care; utilizes research-based evidence and participates in research protocols; develops patient-focused clinical programs; provides staff education; promotes quality care within operating budgetary specifications.
  • Assists physicians in prioritizing his/her work. Gives verbal reminders to physicians of workflow trends and issues or items that need to be completed.
  • Notifies Director of significant occurrences, interventions, or delays.
  • Acts as a liaison between departmental staff, medical personnel, patients and family members. Will assist in any patient care concerns, issues, and complaints.
  • Promotes staff professional growth and development, serving as a mentor, coach, and preceptor to less experienced staff. Provides input to the Manager/Director regarding staff performance and educational needs. Assists with the annual performance review of those staff members.
  • Coordinates and collaborates with other clinical coordinators or team leads in the department.
  • Delegates and assigns additional tasks to staff and oversees their completion, according to professional guidelines and requirements.
  • Ensures shift-to-shift equipment maintenance and stocking of supplies within department rooms/areas by assigning specific staff members and reviewing to ensure tasks have been completed appropriately.
  • Requires completion of incident/occurrence reports regarding unplanned, adverse, or potentially litigious events, per hospital requirements.
  • Receives and gives verbal report on clinical and departmental conditions to and from on/off-going staff.
  • Requires and facilitates handoff process for all patients.
  • Requires and performs walking rounds to ensure safe conditions and availability of equipment and supplies.
  • Provides written shift reports as required to the Manager/Director.
  • Develops policies and procedures for all areas within department.

Leadership Responsibilities

  • Possesses professional and interpersonal communication skills and uses constructive, respectful tones and modes of communication, regardless of the situation.
  • Has the ability and willingness to coach, teach and mentor staff, clinically and professionally.
  • Exhibits verbal and non-verbal support of administrative and departmental quality, customer relations, clinical policies and improvement initiatives and expectations.
  • Provides shift direction during implementation of process changes.
  • Ensures all department staff are using exemplary customer satisfaction techniques and recommends corrections/adjustments as needed
  • Represents departmental leadership in a positive light.
  • Provides guidance and support for staff.
  • Role-modeling teamwork.
  • Provides input to the Manager/Director regarding staff performance and educational needs.
  • Participates in quality and performance improvement initiatives.
  • Attends staff meetings and other required leadership meetings.
  • Facilitates staff meetings and agenda items.
  • Participates in creating schedules for technologists to ensure department's full coverage.
  • Active member in hospital committee’s as needed and ensures that the diagnostic testing department is represented at minimum of 75% of all meetings year.
  • Review quality concerns or variances with staff members and educates as necessary.
  • Assists Leadership team with interview process to ensure new hire appropriateness.
  • Plan and mentor new hires throughout orientation period and acts as a resource after orientation completion.
  • Assists with departmental Super User needs, as required.
  • Weekly review with staff all important updates and news. Coordinates these details with diagnostic testing leadership team.
  • Educational Needs Assessment and creation of plans to ensure staff are educated as necessary.
  • Monitors and provides input for Corrective Action in regards to quality, time, attendance and Patient care within the department.
  • Identify departmental needs and works with Management staff to help meet the needs or determine an appropriate plan of action.
  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.
  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as preceptor, mentor and resource to less experienced staff.
  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards by providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and colleagues.
  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Supplemental Imaging Techonologist Aide
description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. When we say every member of our community, that includes our employees. We know that when our employees feel cared for, heard and valued, they are inspired to create moments that exceed expectations, while prioritizing safety, compassion, personalization and efficiency. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

Position responsible for assisting technologist in performing examinations within the scope of service of the Imaging Department. Assists in all aspects of diagnostic imaging, under the direction of a licensed technologist. Communicates with staff in regards to patient’s needs in a fast paced environment. Maintains adequate supplies in all imaging suites within department. Follows work rules and regulatory requirements. Performs other related duties as requested.

Job Description

Minimum Qualifications

Education: High school diploma or GED; preferred

Licenses/Certification: (None)


An Imaging Aide performing DEXA will need:

  • Sixteen (16) hours of specific bone densitometry equipment training; and
  • Completes four (4) hours of radiation safety and protection training are required in accordance with the State of Texas, annually.

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • Two (2) years of experience in healthcare setting or currently enrolled in an accredited school for Radiologic Technology.
  • Basic computer knowledge in Microsoft Windows and use of electronic mail.
  • Ability to understand written instructions and perform basic mathematical calculations; demonstrates skills for assigned specialty area/function or assigned procedures.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Meets expectations in customer service.
  • Performs advanced direct and indirect patient care, under the direction of an Radiology Tech, as specified in the skills inventory, in a competent manner, according to the needs/age of the patient/population served; assists in planning and implementing direct patient care; documents care provided in patient medical record in accordance with hospital policies/procedures.
  • Assists personnel in meeting patient/family learning needs; maintains communication with healthcare team members to ensure quality of care.
  • Enters physician orders via computer and coordinates schedules of diagnostic testing; assists patients with written teaching protocols; maintains proper stock of linen and all medical and clerical supplies; and assists with technical matters related to PACS, RadNet or other computer based applications.
  • Answers departmental telephones as necessary. Verifies information and resolves common problems.
  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.
  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as preceptor, mentor and resource to less experienced staff.
  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards by providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and colleagues.
  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Director, Product PR
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

We are growing our Global Communications team and hiring a Director of Product PR to own the global Product PR function and shape Snowflake’s AI narrative. This high-impact leadership role drives communications across the company's end-to-end product portfolio, translating complex innovations into compelling stories. You will lead product launches, AI-native partnerships, M&A communications, and executive visibility, including direct C-level communications strategies. We are looking for a strategic powerhouse and modernized media thinker who can seamlessly pivot from advising the C-suite on high-stakes decisions to architecting 360° global campaigns and immersive press experiences.

AS A DIRECTOR OF PRODUCT PR, YOU WILL:

  • Own the Global Product PR Function: Shape Snowflake's AI narrative and drive communications across the end-to-end product portfolio. Translate complex innovations into compelling stories and lead PR for product launches, AI-native partnerships, customer success, and more.

  • Drive Executive Communications: Lead the communications strategy for Snowflake’s product executives, shaping messaging for media interviews, thought leadership, and major product announcements. Develop strategic messaging, keynote narratives, and social content for product leadership.

  • Manage 360° Integrated Campaigns: Lead communications campaign management for Snowflake's highest-priority initiatives, aligning global teams and delivering integrated campaigns spanning corporate, product, executive, customer, partner, analyst, employee, and social communications.

  • Modernize Media Strategy: Expand Snowflake's media footprint beyond traditional outlets, securing visibility across podcasts and Substack. Create high-impact, non-traditional journalist experiences, including curated executive dinners and "speed dating" press sessions.

  • Oversee Flagship Events: Lead communications for major events (Snowflake Summit, BUILD/Expedition, and Snowflake World Tour), driving integrated media programs, executive storytelling, reporter engagement, and press experiences that maximize awareness and business impact.

  • Lead and Develop Talent: Manage, mentor, and inspire a high-functioning team of PR professionals, fostering a high-performance, AI-native culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous growth.

  • Innovate with AI: Build and optimize AI-powered workflows to streamline media monitoring, reporting, content development, and other PR operations, always looking for smarter, faster ways to work.

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

  • 10+ years of experience in public relations, corporate communications, or a related field, with deep expertise in B2B technology and enterprise SaaS.

  • Demonstrated people management experience, with a proven track record of hiring, mentoring, and leading high-performing PR and communications teams.

  • A proven track record of owning global Product PR functions, launching complex technical products, and shaping AI or data narratives.

  • Extensive experience working directly with C-suite executives on strategic communications, keynote development, and high-stakes media engagements.

  • Deep expertise in crisis and issues communications, with the ability to remain calm and strategic while advising senior leadership during sensitive moments.

  • Exceptional writing and storytelling skills, with a talent for translating technical product capabilities into compelling, business-outcome-focused content.

  • A modernized approach to media relations, with strong existing relationships and proven experience leveraging new media (Substack, podcasts) and experiential PR tactics.

  • Experience managing integrated PR for massive-scale tier-one flagship events and global corporate campaigns.

  • A natural curiosity about AI and automation, with demonstrated experience building AI-assisted workflows or integrating new tools into day-to-day work.

  • A bias for action and a builder mentality. You see gaps and fill them without waiting for direction.

  • BA/BS degree or equivalent experience.

This role requires remote and in-office work at our Menlo Park, CA office.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information:

The following represents the expected range of compensation for this role:

  • The estimated base salary range for this role is $228,000 - $299,200.
  • Additionally, this role is eligible to participate in Snowflake’s bonus and equity plan.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. This role is also eligible for a competitive benefits package that includes: medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; flexible spending & health savings account; at least 12 paid holidays; paid time off; parental leave; employee assistance program; and other company benefits.

To comply with pay transparency requirements and other statutes, you can notify us if you believe that a job posting is not compliant by completing this form.

title: SVP, Head of Development Practices & AI Product Development Lifecycle
description:
Lead with Purpose, Unlock Your Team's Passion

At LPL, people leaders hold the key to the employee experience - shaping culture, driving performance, and guiding individuals to new heights. Because when that happens, we all win - clients, LPL, and most importantly, our employees.


If you're ready to lead with intention and discover what's possible, LPL Financial invites you to apply today.


Redefine how enterprise software and digital products are created in an AI-accelerated world. As Head of Development Practices and AI Product Development Lifecycle, you will design the operating model, platforms, guardrails, and team structures that enable smaller, higher-leverage teams to deliver faster while strengthening quality, resilience, security, and accountability.


Job Overview

Reporting directly to the Chief Technology Officer, this senior executive leader will define, lead, and continuously evolve LPL's target-state Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC). The role will embed agentic workflows, autonomous and semi-autonomous agents, and human-in-the-loop governance across discovery, design, development, testing, deployment, operations, and continuous improvement. Working across Engineering, Product, Architecture, Data & AI, Security, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and business leadership, this leader will integrate people, process, platforms, and AI into an observable, auditable, and continuously improving delivery system.


Responsibilities

  • Define and own the target-state AI-native PDLC, including its vision, principles, operating model, stage gates, decision rights, roles, success measures, and multi-year transformation roadmap.
  • Design the target-state team model for AI-augmented product development, including team composition, agent roles, human-agent collaboration patterns, escalation paths, pilot sequencing, scaling criteria, and migration from current delivery structures.
  • Establish enterprise standards for agentic development, including agent taxonomy, workflow orchestration, prompt and context management, tool integration, secure data handling, auditability, and human oversight requirements.
  • Build the PDLC platform and toolchain strategy with Architecture, Platform Engineering, and AI/ML teams across IDE integrations, CI/CD, test automation, observability, knowledge systems, and agent orchestration platforms.
  • Define and govern outcome-based measures for cycle time, release frequency, quality, defect rates, agent utilization and effectiveness, developer experience, cost-to-deliver, technical debt, operational resilience, and business value.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and business leaders to align PDLC adoption with product strategy, portfolio priorities, modernization objectives, and delivery commitments.
  • Embed controls with Enterprise Risk, Information Security, Compliance, Legal, Privacy, and Model Risk Management, ensuring responsible AI use and regulatory readiness throughout the development value stream.
  • Lead organizational transformation and workforce evolution, including role redesign, skills development, hiring strategy, change leadership, performance expectations, coaching, and adoption support for AI-augmented teams.
  • Establish governance and executive reporting for PDLC maturity, adoption, exceptions, risks, investment needs, and realized value; advise senior leadership on technology strategy, organizational design, and competitive implications.
  • Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing leadership team responsible for PDLC strategy, platform enablement, transformation delivery, engineering excellence, and developer experience.

What are we looking for?

We're looking for strong collaborators who deliver exceptional client experiences and thrive in fast-paced, team-oriented environments. Our ideal candidates pursue greatness, act with integrity, and are driven to help our clients succeed. We value those who embrace creativity, continuous improvement, and contribute to a culture where we win together and create and share joy in our work.


Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 15 or more years of progressive leadership experience spanning software engineering, product development, platform engineering, or enterprise technology transformation in large, complex organizations.
  • Proven success leading enterprise-scale delivery transformation, including modern PDLC/SDLC design, DevOps, CI/CD, platform engineering, shift-left quality, operating-model redesign, or product-led delivery.
  • Demonstrated production experience with AI-assisted and agentic development, including large language model coding assistants, agent frameworks, workflow automation, retrieval-augmented generation or knowledge systems, and human oversight.
  • Experience embedding security, privacy, compliance, risk, and audit controls into technology delivery within a regulated or similarly control-intensive environment.

Core Competencies

  • Executive leadership, enterprise influence, strategic planning, and technology investment prioritization
  • End-to-end PDLC design, DevOps, platform engineering, developer experience, quality engineering, and continuous delivery
  • AI-native software development, agent orchestration, prompt and context engineering, automation, and responsible AI governance
  • Team topology, operating-model design, workforce transformation, and change leadership
  • Executive communication, cross-functional partnership, engineering metrics, and outcome-based accountability

Preferences

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
  • Experience in financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry, with direct exposure to secure software development, model risk, privacy, audit, and operational resilience requirements.
  • Cloud, architecture, agile, or DevOps credentials such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Solutions Architect; Certified Scrum Professional; SAFe Practice Consultant; or DevOps Institute certification.


Pay Range:

$240,000.00 - $290,000.00


Actual base salary varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location. Additionally, LPL Total Rewards package is highly competitive, designed to support your success at work, at home, and at play – such as 401K matching, health benefits, employee stock options, paid time off, volunteer time off, and more. Your recruiter will be happy to discuss all that LPL has to offer!


Company Overview:

LPL Financial Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: LPLA) is among the fastest growing wealth management firms in the U.S. As a leader in the financial advisor-mediated marketplace(6) , LPL supports over 32,000 financial advisors and the wealth management practices of approximately 1,100 financial institutions, servicing and custodying approximately $2.3 trillion in brokerage and advisory assets on behalf of approximately 8 million Americans. The firm provides a wide range of advisor affiliation models, investment solutions, fintech tools and practice management services, ensuring that advisors and institutions have the flexibility to choose the business model, services, and technology resources they need to run thriving businesses. For further information about LPL, please visit www.lpl.com.


At LPL, independence means that advisors and institution leaders have the freedom they deserve to choose the business model, services, and technology resources that allow them to run a thriving business. They have the flexibility to do business their way. And they have the freedom to manage their client relationships, because they know their clients best. Simply put, we take care of our advisors and institutions, so they can take care of their clients.


For further information about LPL, please visit .


Join the LPL team and help us make a difference by turning life’s aspirations into financial realities. Please log in or create an account to apply to this position. Principals only. EOE.


Information on Interviews:

LPL will only communicate with a job applicant directly from an @lplfinancial.com email address and will never conduct an interview online or in a chatroom forum. During an interview, LPL will not request any form of payment from the applicant, or information regarding an applicant’s bank or credit card. Should you have any questions regarding the application process, please contact LPL’s Human Resources Solutions Center at (855) 575-6947.

title: Membership Director - AETHOS Lisbon
description:
Join the Aethos Community – Hospitality with Purpose.

At Aethos, we believe in extraordinary places, passionate people, and meaningful connections. Hospitality should inspire and elevate — leaving a lasting impact on mind, body, and soul. That is why we carefully choose our locations and build teams looking for more than just a job — teams that thrive in a true community.

Aethos focuses on sustainability, well-being, and the luxury of time and space. We create retreats from the everyday, offering a sanctuary from the stress of modern life. Our goal? To redefine hospitality — building a place where both guests, members, and team members feel at home, inspired, and connected.

About Aethos Lisbon

Opening in June 2027, Aethos Lisbon will bring our conscious luxury philosophy to the heart of Portugal’s vibrant capital. Blending cultural heritage with modern design, the property will feature an exclusive private members’ club, bespoke wellness and dining spaces, and a thoughtfully curated environment designed to serve as an urban sanctuary for creators, innovators, and mindful travellers.

Join us!

We are looking for an inspiring and strategic Membership Director (m/f) to lead the community vision for Aethos Lisbon. In this role, you will own the membership strategy from the ground up — setting the direction for how members are recruited, welcomed, and retained. You will act as the brand ambassador across the city, overseeing the entire member journey, curating a vibrant calendar of events, and building a balanced, engaged community aligned with our ethos.

Key Mission & Responsibilities

  • Strategy & Commercial Targets: Own the end-to-end membership strategy for the club. Partner closely with the General Manager to turn membership targets into actionable annual plans, budgets, and KPIs, monitoring application, renewal, and engagement metrics to adapt retention strategies.
  • Pre-Opening Outreach & Community Growth: Spearhead outreach before and after our June 2027 launch, actively engaging with Lisbon’s creative, entrepreneurial, and cultural scenes to recruit the founding membership base.
  • Member Acquisition & Onboarding: Oversee the application, assessment, and onboarding standards, ensuring every new member understands the benefits, community values, and opportunities while maintaining a balanced membership profile.
  • The Inner Circle: Build and nurture an active “Inner Circle” programme of influential members and brand advocates who champion the community and introduce high-calibre prospective members.
  • Events & Community Programming: Lead and curate the club’s annual cultural and social events programme, delivering meaningful gatherings that bring members together and reflect the spirit of Aethos Lisbon.
  • Cross-Department Collaboration: Partner with the Marketing Director to align member communications, CRM, and digital storytelling; collaborate across operations, design, wellness, and partnerships to deliver an integrated, flawless club experience.
  • Presence & Relationship Management: Maintain an active, visible presence in the club as the primary welcoming face; oversee guest lists and protocol for VIPs, public figures, and major brand events.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Lead, mentor, and schedule the local membership and events teams, defining core competencies, closing skill gaps through targeted training, and fostering a high-performance culture.
  • Continuous Improvement: Systematically gather member feedback on programming, facilities, and service standards, converting insights into tangible enhancements.

Candidate Profile

  • Experience: Proven senior leadership experience in private members’ clubs, luxury lifestyle hospitality, cultural programming, or high-end community management, including pre-opening or major launch experience.
  • Network & Presence: Deeply connected within Lisbon’s cultural, artistic, culinary, and business ecosystems, with a natural flair for networking and public representation.
  • Strategic & Commercial Acumen: Demonstrated capability in managing budgets, financial targets, data-driven CRM systems, retention strategies, and performance reporting.
  • Personal & Leadership Skills: Charismatic and empathetic communicator, adept at stakeholder management, relationship building, team mentorship, and high-touch member care.
  • Languages: Fluency in English and Portuguese is essential; proficiency in additional languages is a valuable asset.
  • Attitude & Work Style: Entrepreneurial mindset, adaptability, resilience in fast-moving pre-opening phases, and genuine alignment with conscious luxury, wellness, and sustainability.

What We Offer

  • Stability: Full-time executive employment contract.
  • Remuneration: Attractive compensation package reflective of seniority, experience, and the strategic importance of the role.
  • Environment: A key leadership seat in launching a flagship property within a rapidly expanding international boutique brand.
  • Impact & Growth: Direct ownership of a landmark community project with global visibility and long-term career progression opportunities across the Aethos Group.
Ready to shape Lisbon's next cultural sanctuary? We would love to hear from you. Send your CV and cover letter to hr.portugal@aethos.com and dive into your next adventure!

title: SharePoint Developer
description:
About INflow Federal - founded in 2013, INflow Federal is a mission-driven small business delivering cutting-edge solutions to the Department of War (DoW) and Joint Force operations across 20+ states. Our strength comes from our people - especially the Veterans who make up over 50% of our workforce. Through our Veteran Outreach Program and employee-first culture, we invest deeply in professional growth, well-being, and innovation. Known for our agility, transparency, and integrity, INflow combines real-world experience with emerging technologies like AI/ML to help our customers lead in a rapidly evolving defense landscape. We empower both our employees and mission partners to stay ahead - driving smarter, faster, and more secure outcomes.

Job Overview:


INflow Federal is seeking a SharePoint Developer to support our Navy program. NNSY’s mission is to safely return warships to the Fleet on time and within budget. In this role, you will support the design, development, administration, and maintenance of SharePoint and Power Platform solutions that enable enterprise collaboration, workflow automation, and business process modernization.
Here, your work is more than a job—it's a journey in innovation. With opportunities to work on high-impact projects, access to the latest technologies, and a culture that thrives on creativity and collaboration, INflow Federal is where your expertise can truly make a difference.

Job Responsibilities

  • Develop, deploy, and maintain SharePoint solutions, including custom web parts, workflows, lists, libraries, content types, and site collections in both SharePoint Online and SharePoint On-Premises environments.
  • Administer SharePoint environments, including user permissions, security controls, and governance practices.
  • Configure and manage SharePoint sites, document management systems, and collaboration solutions.
  • Utilize SharePoint Designer, InfoPath, and Power Automate to design and automate workflows.
  • Design, develop, and maintain Power Apps solutions, including both Canvas apps and Model-driven apps.
  • Create and manage Power Automate workflows to streamline business processes and integrate with data sources such as SQL, SharePoint, and third-party APIs.
  • Connect Power Apps solutions to multiple data sources, leveraging Common Data Service (Dataverse) and implementing business rules within applications.
  • Develop client-side solutions using the SharePoint Framework (SPFx).
  • Utilize modern JavaScript frameworks such as React or Angular in conjunction with SharePoint and Power Apps.
  • Develop custom SharePoint and Power Apps integrations using REST APIs, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and jQuery.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues within SharePoint and Power Apps environments, including performance optimization, error diagnosis, and remediation.
  • Perform routine system maintenance and updates to ensure the stability, security, and availability of SharePoint and Power Apps solutions.

Required Skills

  • Proven experience developing, deploying, and maintaining SharePoint solutions in both SharePoint Online and SharePoint On-Premises environments
  • Strong experience administering SharePoint environments, including permissions, security controls, and governance practices
  • Hands-on expertise designing and developing Power Apps solutions (Canvas and Model-driven apps)
  • Proficiency creating and managing Power Automate workflows to streamline and integrate business processes
  • Experience developing client-side SharePoint solutions using SPFx and modern JavaScript frameworks (e.g., React or Angular)
  • Ability to integrate SharePoint and Power Platform solutions with multiple data sources, including Dataverse, SQL, REST APIs, and third-party services

title: Talent Advisor
description:
We are looking for a high-energy Talent Advisor to join our National Banking program and drive the full-cycle recruitment engine for a world-class financial brand. This is a fast-paced, high-impact role where you’ll act as a strategic partner to hiring managers, delivering an elite candidate experience while owning the "sprint" velocity of a major launch!
join the world’s most equitable and specialized talent company

Are you our new colleague? We’re looking for a

Talent Advisor

how you will contribute

As a Talent Advisor, you will serve as a strategic and consultative partner to our client’s Key Stakeholders and Hiring Managers. You are ultimately responsible for the fulfillment of requisitions, taking full accountability and ownership of results to ensure client needs and market conditions are met. You will collaborate with global colleagues—including Sourcing Specialists and Centers of Expertise—to execute talent strategies that produce quality hires.

your typical day includes

  • Consulting with Stakeholders: Performing intake calls to clarify positions beyond the job description and managing expectations regarding timelines.
  • Strategy Execution: Acting as an advisor on sourcing strategies and gathering market intelligence to share with hiring managers.
  • Pipeline Management: Managing the candidate pool, including internal, ad response, and direct sourced candidates.
  • Candidate Engagement: Using influence and persuasion to sell opportunities, extending offers, and negotiating to final acceptance.
  • Performance Tracking: Monitoring your performance scorecard to ensure all SLAs and KPIs are consistently met or exceeded.

your responsibilities include

  • Serving as the single point of contact for Hiring Managers on all assigned requisitions.
  • Evaluating and reprioritizing employment branding strategies.
  • Using independent judgment to determine candidate eligibility based on resumes and interviews.
  • Building qualified candidate profiles and presenting slates to meet client deliverables.
  • Protecting the candidate experience and fostering strong partnerships across boundaries.

your background

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree or 4 years of equivalent work experience.
  • Experience: Minimum of 3 years in account management or consultative recruiting as a primary point of contact.
  • Sourcing Expertise: Minimum of 5 years in a candidate generation role with a proven track record of hiring success.
  • Environment: Experience in high-pressure, urgent recruiting environments (e.g., RPO, Search Firm, or Agency).

key capabilities

  • Technical Proficiency: Skilled in Microsoft Office (Excel, PPT, Word, Outlook), Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), and CRM systems.
  • Strategic Thinking: Ability to translate functional/technical hiring needs into effective candidate generation strategies.
  • Communication: Proven ability to build productive relationships and consult with all levels of an organization

together we grow.

When you join Randstad, you join…

  • A specialized team delivering tailored solutions for clients and talent, enabling meaningful impact.
  • An equitable, inclusive culture where everyone can contribute and thrive.
  • A workplace prioritizing growth and empowering teams to adapt and excel.
  • A company dedicated to supporting you to perform at your best.
  • A commitment to pay for performance with transparency, fairness, and competitiveness

our purpose

Our purpose is deeply rooted in the belief that by knowing our clients and talent better than anyone else, we can make connections that change lives and transform businesses. We don’t just place people in jobs; we help create futures full of possibility — for our clients, talent, and communities.

our culture

Our culture is powered by ambition and collaboration, where everyone is driven to push boundaries and achieve success. At Randstad, we don’t settle for “good enough” — we’re committed to walking the extra mile, always striving for perfection while trusting each other to deliver results. You’ll be working in an environment that fosters both individual achievement and team success.

We want our teams and talent to reflect the rich diversity of the societies we serve. We thrive for an environment of belonging, safety and confidence. So everyone can bring their whole selves to work and flourish. Learn more about equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging at Randstad here.

leadership expectations

At Randstad, leadership is our shared language. Whether you are leading a team or driving your own career, you contribute to our goal of being the world's most equitable and specialized talent company. We lead across four core pillars:

  1. we set direction: it is about anticipating and making decisions that will position Randstad for long term success.
  2. we achieve: it is about delivering on our goals and operational excellence.
  3. we care: it is about the way we collaborate and work together, creating a sustainable and healthy culture.
  4. lead by example: it is about modelling the behaviors and standards we expect from others, demonstrating courage and accountability in every action.

a place for you to grow

We provide a fast-paced growth environment where your ability to adapt and contribute fuels the success of both your team and clients. We appreciate your talents and support your growth through mentorship, skill-building, and career guidance.

meaningful, competitive, and equitable rewards for your performance.

Our employment conditions reflect this;

  • competitive salary
  • variable pay for performance
  • growth and development opportunities in a fast changing global environment
  • an environment that promotes work life balance: flexibility with intentionality.

If you recognize yourself in the profile above, we invite you to apply for this role.

The recruitment procedure consists of a screening and at least two interviews. Later in the process, an (online) assessment and a job offer conversation take place.

Working at Randstad is unlike working at any organization. Because at Randstad we put people at the heart of everything we do. This goes for our clients, our talent, our employees and society. We combine our passion for people with the power of today’s technologies. This helps us support people and organizations in realizing their true potential. Learn more about our mission, history and values on our website:

At Randstad, we know employees that are cared for holistically have the confidence to bring their fullest potential to work, so we make investments in our people.

The base salary range for this position is $62,400-$74,880.

Pay offered to a successful candidate will be based on several factors including the candidate’s education, work experience, work location, specific job duties, certifications, etc. Based on eligibility, a successful candidate’s total compensation may include a variable pay plan including bonus(es) and/or commission(s). In setting compensation, Randstad complies with all local wage and hour laws and while the pay range listed above is an annual amount, non-exempt employees will be paid hourly and therefore receive the hourly equivalent.

In addition, Randstad offers rich learning & development opportunities, as well as a competitive benefit package.

title: Intermediate Interior Designer (Institutional)
description:
Here at DIALOG, we are passionate about design and believe it can and should meaningfully improve the wellbeing of our communities and the environment we all share.
We are a multi-disciplinary practice of architects, interior designers, urban designers and planners, structural, mechanical and electrical engineers, landscape architects and sustainability experts who design for community wellbeing and urban vibrancy. We are a fun-loving bunch of big thinkers and city-shapers, who are collaborative in our approach, diverse in our perspectives, aspirational in our pursuits, and optimistic about what’s next. We’re always looking for passionate people who share our values and care as much about our communities as we do. We're proud to be a Certified B Corporation and one of Canada's Greenest Employers, committed to using our design practice as a force for good in the world.

We’re looking for an Intermediate Interior Designer to join our award-winning institutional interior design team in DIALOG’s Toronto studio. Working across post-secondary, civic and healthcare projects, we create thoughtful, inclusive environments that respond to the people and communities they serve.

Our team combines creative design thinking with technical rigour and a collaborative approach. We work closely with clients and users to understand their needs, translate them into a clear design vision, and carry that vision through detailing, documentation and construction.

You’ll join a team of interior designers who care deeply about their work, enjoy collaborating and bring energy and enthusiasm to the design process. We share ideas openly, support one another and celebrate our successes together. You’ll contribute to large, complex projects, take ownership of your work and grow your design and technical capabilities within a team that values curiosity, shared knowledge and attention to detail.

How you'll make a difference:

  • Contribute to client and user engagement, visioning and functional programming to understand project needs and inform the design.
  • Develop interior design concepts, space plans, material palettes and details that respond to each project’s vision, users and operational requirements.
  • Prepare compelling presentations, including material boards, renderings, and 2D and 3D design drawings, to communicate ideas to clients and project teams.
  • Develop coordinated drawings, schedules and specifications from schematic design through construction documents.
  • Collaborate with architecture, engineering and other disciplines to integrate interior design throughout the project.
  • Select and specify materials, finishes, furniture and equipment, and prepare furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E) documentation.
  • Apply building code, accessibility and project requirements to support safe, inclusive and functional environments.
  • Support construction administration through shop drawing and submittal reviews, responses to requests for information, site visits and field reviews.
  • Participate in deficiency reviews and furniture installation reviews to support the successful completion of projects.

Who you are:

  • An interior designer with 5–8 years of relevant experience, including work on institutional projects such as post-secondary, civic or healthcare facilities.
  • A graduate of a bachelor’s degree program in interior design or a related field (NCIDQ certification is an asset).
  • A thoughtful designer with a strong portfolio demonstrating conceptual thinking, space planning, material selection and attention to detail.
  • Experienced in developing technical drawings and coordinating interior design within large, complex buildings.
  • Proficient in Revit and Adobe Creative Suite, with experience in 3D modelling and visualization (Blender, SketchUp or Rhino experience is an asset).
  • Able to translate a design vision into thoughtful, functional spaces and well-resolved details.
  • Attentive and thorough, with a commitment to coordinated documentation and quality project delivery.
  • Interested in universal design, sustainability and the relationship between the built environment and wellbeing.
  • A dependable collaborator who takes ownership of your work, communicates priorities and challenges, and contributes to shared project goals.
  • Comfortable building relationships with clients, consultants and colleagues through listening, clear communication and follow-through.
  • Generous in sharing knowledge, receptive to feedback and motivated to grow within a supportive team.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Don’t meet every single requirement? We still encourage you to apply! We’re looking for future DIALOGers who are eager to learn, bring unique perspectives, and want to make a real difference in the world—even if your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification.
Perks & Benefits
Parental leave top-up programs for all parents upon the birth or adoption of a child, RRSP matching, competitive medical and dental benefits coverage upon the first day of employment, discounted memberships, encouraged work/life balance with gifted time off during the holiday season and Vacation Buy-Up program, and reimbursement for professional memberships and dues are just a few of the benefits that DIALOGers enjoy.
Professional Development
DIALOG offers continued professional growth through leadership development opportunities specifically designed for our collaborative culture. Among others, some of our programs include: CoachDIALOG which equips our coaches with essential communication and feedback strategies for building great teams; Integrateducation™ supports DIALOGers in accredited continuing education opportunities; technical skills development via e-learning pathways; and financial support for relevant external learning opportunities.
Equal Opportunity
DIALOG celebrates diversity and is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to an inclusive environment for all, free of discrimination and harassment. Employment-related decisions are made without regard to sex, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, age and race. In accordance with DIALOG’s Accommodation Policy, accommodations for people with disabilities are available upon request for candidates throughout the selection process.

title: Distribution Center Assistant Supervisor
description:

In the absence of the Distribution Center Supervisor will be responsible for all aspects of the job tasks within their department.

title: X Ray Technician Limited Scope $2500 sign on bonus
description:
Overview

$2500 sign on bonus

Hours: 8a-5p Monday through Friday

Location:

2011 S Texas Ave Bryan, TX 77802

Are you ready to take your career to new heights? At Concentra, you will be a vital member of our patient care team and play a crucial role in providing exceptional care to our patients. Our mission is to improve the health of America's workforce, one patient at a time. Join us at Concentra and see how your clinical competency and compassion can make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients you serve.

The X Ray Limited Scope & Medical Support Specialist performs routine x-ray, medical, and testing procedures under direct supervision of the treating clinician as well as supports in other areas of the facility as needed including registration and referral management. This position will also perform routine X-ray examinations in accordance with Concentra policies, practices, and procedures and applicable regulations. This role requires efficient and accurate delivery of one-on-one patient care while thriving in a fast-paced environment. Also will ensure that every patient is treated with quality clinical care and receives an excellent patient experience from welcoming, respectful, and skillful colleagues.

Responsibilities

X-ray Technician Duties

  • Prepare patients for radiologic procedures. Escort patients to dressing and x-ray rooms, provide verbal and/or written instructions and assist patients in positioning body parts to be radiographed. Explain procedures and observe patients to ensure patient care, safety and comfort during the x-ray exam
  • Operate radiologic equipment to produce images of the body for diagnostic purposes. Position radiologic equipment and adjust controls to set exposure time and distance according to specification of examination. Take x-rays following established radiologic requirements and regulations to ensure patient care and safety
  • Use radiation safety measures and protection devices to ensure safety of patients and team members
  • Ensure radiologic equipment remains in working order. Report equipment malfunctions to Center Operations Director
  • Ensure all Radiology workflows are followed and all Radiology reports cross correctly to EMRFollows documentation procedures and completes required documentation related to patient x-ray visit.
  • Maintain all x-ray equipment, including calibration, QA/QC procedures, and record keeping in accordance with current policy and procedures

Medical Support Specialist Duties

  • Perform Department of Transportation (DOT) and Non-DOT drug and alcohol testing
  • Prepare patients for physical examinations, including taking vital signs and any required or requested ancillary testing including but not limited to vaccines and injections, phlebotomy, PFTs, audiogram testing and respirator fit testing
  • Perform rapid screening tests (influenza, strep, mono, glucose, etc.)
  • Assist providers during examination and treatment
  • Responsible for performing routine medical procedures as ordered by treating clinician as well as triaging emergent patients as needed
  • Prepare and assist clinician with procedure set up and injury care
  • Apply bandages, dressings and splints as ordered by the treating clinician
  • Dispense medications and DME as ordered by the treating clinician in accordance with state regulations
  • Complete quality assurance activities on equipment and medical devices as well as testing processes used in the center
  • Maintain supplies, clean rooms and equipment, and stock exam rooms
  • Maintain and operate all medical devices and equipment, including calibration and record keeping in accordance with current policy and procedures
  • Notify supervisor immediately if equipment is not functioning properly, supplies are needed, or facility is not operating as expected
  • In partnership with center leadership, assist with patient flow and volume
  • Keep patients informed of expected wait times during all aspects of the center visit
  • Responsible for clerical tasks in both the front and back office associated with patient care and proper record keeping
  • Ensure accuracy in documentation
  • Perform front office duties: greet patients, obtain authorization, check in/out, communicate wait times, answer multi-line telephone system, and distribute employer results/paperwork as needed
  • Follow HIPAA guidelines and safety rules
  • Attend center staff meetings or huddles as required
  • Assist in maintaining a neat, clean, and orderly appearance throughout the facility
  • Complete any applicable training including but not limited to clinical competency training that occurs monthly.

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

  • High school graduate or GED equivalent
  • Certifications and/or Licenses:
  • Completion of state approved Limited Scope Technician certificate program and license by the state in which employed, if applicable.
  • CPR/First Aid Certification

Job-Related Experience

  • Customarily has at least six months or more of medical assistant experience with knowledge of medical procedures and medical terminology
  • Customarily has at least six months of demonstrated experience in X-Ray and familiarity with routine medical procedures
  • Working knowledge of occupational medicine requirements (state specific) is preferred with prior medical office, healthcare and/or customer service-related experience.

Job-Related Skills/Competencies

  • Concentra Core Competencies of Service Mentality, Attention to Detail, Sense of Urgency, Initiative and Flexibility
  • Ability to make decisions or solve problems by using logic to identify key facts, explore alternatives, and propose quality solutions
  • Outstanding customer service skills as well as the ability to deal with people in a manner which shows tact and professionalism
  • The ability to properly handle sensitive and confidential information (including HIPAA and PHI) in accordance with federal and state laws and company policies
  • Able to communicate both verbally and in writing in a clear, and professional manner
  • Teamwork focus with peers and center leadership team; ability to maintain working relationship with all levels of colleagues
  • Must participate in initial and ongoing training as required
  • Obtain all certifications required of Medical Support Specialists including but not limited to Drug Screen Collection, Breath Alcohol Certification, Hair and Oral Fluids Collection
  • Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel, Outlook and entry of data into various systems/applications

Additional Data

  • Life & Disability Insurance

  • Colleague Referral Bonus Program

title: 12-Month Placement Programme, Private Client Tax - Southampton (July 2027)
description:
Why S&W?

At S&W, we believe a great early career experience is about more than just the work you do. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that help shape your future. Whether that's developing new skills, growing your confidence or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that supports you to be yourself and succeed.

During your 12 month placement you'll contribute to meaningful work, learn from experienced professionals and gain first-hand insight into life in professional services.

As one of the UK's fastest-growing accountancy and advisory firms, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. Your placement is a chance to experience life at S&W first-hand, get to know our people and culture, and explore what a future career with us could look like.

We see our placement students as future talent, which is why many go on to secure a place on one of our Graduate programmes after completing their degree.

No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required. We're looking for people who are curious, motivated and eager to learn. What matters most is your attitude, potential and willingness to get involved.

The Private Client Tax Team at S&W

Our Private Client Tax Services team helps individuals from all walks of life with their tax affairs. With over 6,000 private tax clients and 1,500 trusts, our client base is incredibly diverse, ranging from high-net-worth individuals and families to entrepreneurs, business owners and family businesses.

You will be joining a team that supports clients in meeting their tax compliance obligations and liaises with HMRC on their behalf. This can include preparing tax returns, repayment claims, computations and accounts, as well as managing correspondence with HMRC.

What will you be doing?

The Private Client Tax Internship will give you valuable insight into life within a professional services firm and provide hands-on experience of the work our graduates undertake on a day-to-day basis. You could be attending meetings with partners, assisting with client work or supporting research projects. There will be a wide variety of work to get involved in, giving you the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution as part of the team.

Over the course of the placement, you'll gain valuable insight into life at S&W, develop professional skills, expand your network and build a deeper understanding of the opportunities available in Audit & Assurance.

You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from support from colleagues across the business, giving you the opportunity to learn from people at different stages of their careers and build connections that last beyond the programme.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Liaising with clients and third parties to obtain the information required to support tax compliance and advisory work.
  • Preparing basic tax returns and repayment claim forms.
  • Assisting with the preparation of tax advice for clients, including conducting technical tax research, supporting strategic planning and drafting client reports.
  • Managing correspondence with clients, HMRC and other third parties via letter, email and telephone.

You'll be someone who:

  • Is naturally curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges
  • Communicates well, builds positive relationships and collaborates effectively with others
  • Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems
  • Is organised, willing to take ownership and able to manage competing priorities
  • Is interested in understanding how businesses operate and the challenges they face

You'll also need to:

  • Be available to start on 28th June 2027
  • Be in your penultimate year of university
  • Be on track to achieve at least a 2:2 degree in any discipline
  • Have a minimum of 112 UCAS points from your top three A Levels (or equivalent), excluding General Studies
  • Have achieved a minimum Grade 5 (or equivalent) in GCSE English Language and Maths

No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required, and we welcome applications from all degree disciplines.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.

We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know.

IMPORTANT NOTES FOR COMPLETING YOUR APPLICATION

When you click on the 'I'm interested' button, you'll be taken to your profile page. We're currently updating it, but in the meantime:

  • We can only accept one application to any of our programmes in a recruitment season. If you're unsuccessful, you'll need to wait until the following recruitment season to reapply.
  • Under the Resume (CV) section, uploading a document is mandatory; however, it will not be formally reviewed.

title: Canvassing Director
description:

description:

WEB stands for Where Everyone Belongs. It is a school community program for 8th graders only, that helps students feel welcomed, connected, and included.

WEB members serve as role models and peer leaders, welcoming new students, building friendships, and helping everyone at South feel part of the school.

A WEB Advisor helps create a welcoming, inclusive environment where every student feels seen, valued, and connected. Through guidance, advocacy, and community-building, the WEB Advisor helps students feel they have a place and people who care.

TYPE OF POSITION:

• Extracurricular
• After school hours; specific hrs/days to be determined

Activities Director, Building Principals

None

$3,426 - $4,315 (depending on experience)

An Advisor works with students to teach and refine leadership skills in peer environments, and assist students with decision-making in building wide activities and events.

title: Art Director
description:
Hermeus is a venture-backed defense aviation company reclaiming the lost art of rapid iterative prototyping to build the fastest aircraft in the world today. By prioritizing relentless hardware iteration, we deliver high-speed systems at the pace of the modern battlefield. We work with the Department of War to provide the high-speed capabilities our nation and its allies need to maintain a durable, asymmetric advantage.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a versatile Art Director to support our creative team on a contract basis, working approximately two days per week. You will be responsible for defining visual and tonal guidelines, shaping storytelling strategies, and conceptualizing engaging brand content across PR and editorial channels, while also helping the executive leadership team with key assets.

This person will take projects through final delivery, operating as both a high-level strategist and a hands-on creator to ensure all output beautifully delivers against both performance and brand objectives while maintaining a consistent visual standard.

Contract Details
  • Schedule: 16 hours/week, Monday–Friday
  • Contract Duration: 3-6 months

Responsibilities:

  • Define and evolve visual and tonal guidelines to ensure consistency across all brand touchpoints.
  • Shape storytelling strategies and conceptualize engaging brand content specifically tailored for PR and editorial channels.
  • Partner directly with executive leadership to design, produce, and refine high-impact executive assets.
  • Conceptualize, design, and lead the end-to-end development of high-quality still and moving creative assets for both paid and organic marketing channels.
  • Help manage relationships with external agencies, creative partners, and freelancers for larger projects.

Requirements:

  • Proven professional experience as an Art Director, Designer, or in a similar creative role, with a strong balance of strategy and hands-on execution.
  • A robust portfolio showcasing strong conceptual thinking, typography, layout design, and brand identity work.
  • Mastery of industry-standard design tools.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to articulate creative rationale and take feedback constructively.
  • Reliable availability to work approximately two days per week on a contract basis.

The range listed for this role is intended as a general guideline. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including role scope and responsibilities, relevant experience, education and training, key skills, market data, and business needs.

At Hermeus, compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. We offer competitive pay, and a range of benefits designed to support our team.

Benefits:

  • Time Off: Eligible for unpaid time off and up to 5 days of sick leave.
  • Office Perks: Weekly paid office lunches and fully stocked breakrooms.

The person hired will have access to information and items subject to U.S. export controls, and therefore, must either be a “U.S. person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. § 120.62 or otherwise eligible for deemed export licensing. US persons include U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), and asylees and refugees with such status granted, not pending.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY
Hermeus is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
