title: Senior Director - Disclosures Strategy
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

Veeva Systems is seeking an accomplished and driven Senior Director of Strategy to drive the adoption and growth of our clinical trial disclosures and transparency solution, Veeva Disclosures, within the Veeva Clinical Operations suite.
This strategic leader will be responsible for defining, building, and driving the market adoption and growth of our industry-leading Disclosures solution. The ideal candidate possesses a deep blend of strategy, commercial execution, and knowledge of clinical trial transparency and disclosure practices within the Life Sciences industry. This role requires the ability to operate at an executive strategy level while simultaneously driving detailed, cross-functional execution to streamline how sponsors and CROs meet their global trial registration and results reporting obligations.

What You'll Do

  • Drive Go-to-Market Strategy - Develop and execute comprehensive strategies to increase adoption and usage of Veeva Disclosures among Life Sciences companies (Sponsors, CROs, and emerging biotechs), aligning with Veeva’s broader Clinical Operations and Development Cloud vision
  • Engage with Customers - Act as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert to executive stakeholders, articulating the measurable value of a connected disclosures solution in improving registration speed, submission accuracy, deadline management, and overall transparency reporting efficiency
  • Support Sales Teams - Partner deeply with Veeva’s sales organization to define target accounts, educate customers on the advantages of a modern, cloud-native disclosures application that sources data directly from their existing clinical applications, support strategic sales cycles, and ensure revenue goals are achieved
  • Industry Thought Leadership - Represent Veeva as the primary evangelist for clinical trial transparency technology at key industry events, conferences, and executive customer meetings to drive awareness, define market opportunity, and establish credibility
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration - Work closely with Veeva’s Product Management, Marketing, and Services teams to refine core positioning and messaging, shape the future Disclosures roadmap based on market demand, and ensure seamless delivery and customer success
  • Market Insights & Feedback - Continuously gather detailed customer feedback on disclosure and transparency pain points, identify emerging trends in global registry requirements and public data sharing, and provide actionable insights to enhance the Disclosures product and overall business strategy

Requirements

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in strategic leadership, business development, or product/go-to-market strategy, specifically within a clinical software/SaaS/PaaS environment
  • Proven Operator: A track record as a successful leader who can seamlessly transition between high-level strategy and detailed execution/project management
  • Exceptional Communication: Strong presentation skills with the ability to articulate complex operational and technical concepts to diverse audiences (technical teams, clinical operations leaders, and C-level executives)
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required

Nice to Have

  • Disclosures Domain Expertise: Deep experience leading go-to-market strategy for clinical trial disclosure and transparency solutions; understanding the nuances of trial registration, results reporting, and redaction and anonymization workflows is a core competency
  • Clinical Operations Expertise: Specific experience with the operational workflows of sponsor clinical development, transparency, and regulatory teams, as well as CROs
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Familiarity with GCP, ICH guidelines, and global clinical trial transparency requirements such as ClinicalTrials.gov and EU CTR
  • Advanced Degree: MBA or advanced degree in a related field is a plus

Interviewing with Veeva

We value your time and believe in a transparent hiring process. Here is the process you can expect.
  • Follow the application process and submit your resume.
  • If moving to the interview stage, our process is as follows:
    1. A conversation with the hiring manager
    2. A personality assessment (unless you have already completed it with Veeva previously)
    3. A practical case exercise
    4. A final conversation with our group's Senior Leader
  • Once all interviews are complete, the manager will be in touch with a final decision.

Perks & Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
  • Flexible PTO and company paid holidays
  • Retirement programs
  • 1% charitable giving program

Compensation

  • Base pay: $150,000 - $300,000
  • The salary range listed here has been provided to comply with local regulations and represents a potential base salary range for this role. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range above or below, depending on experience and location. title: Waste Water Analyst
description:
Tate & Lyle is a global provider of ingredients and solutions to the food, beverage, and other industries, operating from more than 30 locations around the world. The ingredients and solutions add taste, texture, nutrition, and increased functionality to products that millions of people around the world use or consume every day. We are the secret ingredient to make food extraordinary in some of the world’s best loved brands.


ROLE PURPOSE:

The WWTP lab technician is responsible for the physical tests performed on various samples retrieved from both the WWTP and production facility. This includes equalization tank, UASB, SBR, disk filter, production plant flume, stills bottoms, etc. Accuracy in testing and reporting is essential. Required to work alone during night shift, holidays, and weekends. Must be able to work 12-hour shifts.

SAFETY ACCOUNTABILITIES – EHSQ CRITICAL ROLE LEVEL 3

Each team member is expected to support the Tate & Lyle culture where Environment, Health, Food Safety and Quality, complies with all EHSQ policies, procedures, and regulations relevant to their work. Team members are expected to speak up and intervene to prevent unsafe conditions and to respect fellow workers and the communities in which we work. Included in this is abidance with our Life Saving Principles (LSP’s) and our STOP WORK AUTHORITY which are developed to strengthen our workplace safety, prevent serious injury loss of life. Responsible for quality and food safety within their realm of control.

Level 3 – Important Role

  • EHSQ focus is 100% task oriented
  • Responsible for area specific EHSQ procedures/policy adherence
  • EHSQMS Element Support
  • Responsible for reporting all incidents, defects, and hazards
  • Involved in EHSQ specific checks and inspections for policy adherence

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES:

Works independently to retrieve and properly label samples.

  • Prepares samples by following documented procedures. Must have physical ability to manipulate 5-gallon containers of liquid weighing approximately 40 pounds 30 feet and locate on shelves 6 feet above the floor. Required to utilize acids and bases and other commonly used chemicals in the laboratory. (Containers are labelled for identification). Required to calibrate equipment and maintain accurate records.

Tests wastewater samples.

  • Required to perform physical and analytical tests on various samples including but not limited to UASB, SBR, Final Effluent, and impoundments. Must be able to coordinate work responsibilities independently and report timely and accurate results. Generally, WWTP lab technician responsibilities require up to 10 hours of each shift to be spent on your feet. In addition, the job requires manual dexterity to make fine measurements with lab equipment, basic math skills to calculate test results, and the ability to learn basic computer skills to enter data.

Compliance Tasks.

  • Daily testing of pH and DO, weekly testing of TRO. Ensure that chain of custody (COC) is filled out correctly for compliance samples. Escalating any out of compliance or abnormal operating parameters to WWTP supervisor or Area Manager.

Daily clean-up of glassware and utensils after use.

  • Used glassware and utensils are collected at the sink area for hand washing, and washing is accomplished by working at a waist-high counter and sink. After cleaning is completed, each piece of glassware and/or utensils is placed in wall cabinets or in drawers under the counter.

OTHER (MARGINAL) TASKS:

  • Rounds of the facility are completed on a routine basis looking for leaks or other problems that could result in environmental permit non-compliance. Routine cleaning of the grounds, control room, lab, and restroom facilities are completed on a routine basis. Monitoring of reagent and chemical inventories and assisting with ordering. Light maintenance (PM completion, cleaning of the heat exchangers, changing tubing, etc.)

FOOD, ENVIRONMENT, HEALTH & SAFETY DUTY OF CARE:

Food Safety:

  • Carry out responsibilities/duties according to food safety, legal and quality requirements to ensure that our products are fit for human consumption

Environment:

  • Comply with all environmental standards, procedures, and work instructions always.
  • Report any environmental violation or near misses to prevent any impact upon the local environment, its inhabitants and Tate & Lyle

Health & Safety:

  • Adhere to the safety policies, procedures, and site rules
  • Fully participate in the safety program, including reporting any incidents or near misses and auditing

SKILLS, TRAINING and EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

  • High School Diploma/GED Required. Associate’s degree Preferred.
  • Must qualify to obtain and hold proper certification from Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality.
  • A minimum of one-year prior wastewater treatment plant work experience is preferred.
  • Must be physically capable of performing the duties of the position.
  • Must be able to learn basic computer skills.
  • Must have demonstrated the ability to learn to perform the duties of the position in a reasonable amount of time.

The Company is committed to complying with the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) and all data privacy and laws in the jurisdictions in which it recruits and hires employees. PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. title: Weld Inspector

Job Purpose

To support the continued growth in Fabrication Projects, the Belfast Operations team have an opportunity for a Level 2 Welding Inspector to join their team on a full-time basis.     • Cracking
    • Porosity
    • Undercut
    • Lack of fusion
    • Slag inclusions
    • Overlap
    • Excessive reinforcement
  • Ensure compliance with approved:
    • Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS)
    • Inspection & Test Plans (ITP)
    • Engineering drawings
    • Client specifications
    • Applicable codes and standards
  • Complete inspection reports and quality documentation accurately.
  • Maintain weld traceability records and inspection logs.
  • Record non-conformances and assist with corrective actions.
  • Verify material identification and heat number traceability where required.
  • Support compilation of Client quality documentation packs and MRB’s.
  • Liaise with welders and supervisors regarding quality concerns and repair requirements.
  • Monitor fabrication activities to ensure compliance with procedures and standards.
  • Participate in weld repair verification and reinspection activities.
  • Assist with coordination of NDT activities where required.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives relating to welding quality and productivity.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Knowledge of: --

  • Welding processes:
    • FCAW
    • GMAW/MIG
    • SMAW
    • GTAW/TIG
    • SAW
  • Fabrication and welding practices
  • Welding symbols and engineering drawings
  • Dimensional inspection techniques
  • Common welding codes and standards such as:
    • ISO 3834
    • EN 1090
    • ISO 5817
    • Lloyds Register
    • IACS

Education and Experience

  • BTEC/NVQ 3 in related engineering discipline
  • CSWIP 3.1 / PCN level 2 Welding Inspector
  • Understanding/experience of shipbuilding classification rules and specifications
  • Strong knowledge of welding techniques, materials and industry standards

  • Good level of IT experience using Microsoft word and excel

    • A collaborative and supportive working environment.

title: MI/Workflow Officer
description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Senior MI & Transformation Manager, the MI & Workflow Senior Officer will support the development, production and continuous improvement of management information for the Client Onboarding and KYC department. The role will have a primary focus on accurate, timely and insightful reporting covering onboarding volumes, KYC activity, workflow performance, backlogs, service levels, capacity and operational risks. It will also support the effective management of workflows, operational trackers and data controls, while contributing to transformation initiatives and technology-led improvements that simplify, standardise and automate reporting and operational processes. This will include supporting requirements gathering, testing, implementation and adoption to ensure cases are recorded and progressed consistently and that management information is reliable.

The successful candidate will help deliver business-as-usual reporting, respond to emerging MI requirements and contribute to transformation initiatives across Client Onboarding and KYC. They will work closely with onboarding analysts, team leaders, managers and key stakeholders to improve reporting, workflow visibility, data quality and the use of MI in operational decision-making. The role will help provide assurance that onboarding and KYC work is visible, consistently tracked and supported by clear information, while escalating emerging risks, control gaps or delays to the Senior MI Manager.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the Senior MI Manager with the design, development, production and maintenance of management information and operational reporting.
  • Produce accurate and timely daily, weekly, monthly and ad hoc BAU reports, ensuring agreed definitions, controls and reporting deadlines are consistently applied.
  • Analyse operational data to identify trends, backlogs, capacity pressures, service-level risks, exceptions and opportunities for improvement.
  • Produce and maintain MI for the Client Onboarding and KYC department, including case volumes, status and ageing, turnaround times, service-level performance, backlogs, quality outcomes, risk indicators and team capacity.
  • Maintain, develop and govern workflow tools and operational trackers so that work is recorded consistently and progress, ownership, status and actions are clear.
  • Monitor workflow data and tracker completion, challenge gaps or inconsistencies and work with teams to improve data quality and compliance with agreed processes.
  • Support consistent use of Client Onboarding and KYC workflows and trackers, ensuring key stages, ownership, outstanding information, approvals, risk matters and completion outcomes are captured accurately.
  • Document reporting logic, data definitions, controls and procedures to create a clear audit trail and support consistent, repeatable reporting.
  • Support the testing, implementation and embedding of reporting, workflow and automation improvements delivered through transformation initiatives.
  • Actively contribute to Client Onboarding and KYC transformation initiatives by helping to define requirements, assess current processes and identify opportunities to simplify, standardise and automate reporting and workflows.
  • Work with technology teams, product owners and operational stakeholders to support the design, testing, implementation and adoption of system enhancements, digital tools and technology-led improvements, ensuring solutions deliver reliable data, effective controls and measurable operational benefits.
  • Work with operational teams and stakeholders to gather requirements, translate them into practical MI or workflow solutions and communicate findings clearly.
  • Provide cover and resilience for key reporting activities, manage competing priorities and escalate data, workflow or delivery risks promptly.

Skills, Experience & Qualifications

  • Experience producing and maintaining operational MI, dashboards, recurring reports and ad hoc analysis in a business or operational environment.
  • Strong Excel skills, including data cleansing, formulas, lookups, pivot tables and the presentation of clear, accurate information. Experience with Power BI, Power Query or similar reporting tools is desirable.
  • Experience maintaining workflow systems, case-management data, SharePoint or Microsoft Lists, operational trackers or comparable tools.
  • Ability to analyse data, identify trends and exceptions, investigate inconsistencies and explain the operational impact in clear language.
  • Strong attention to detail and experience applying data-quality checks, reconciliations, version control and documented reporting definitions.
  • Ability to manage recurring deadlines alongside ad hoc requests, prioritise effectively and provide dependable cover for critical reporting.
  • Good stakeholder-management skills, with the confidence to gather requirements, challenge incomplete information and present findings appropriately.
  • Experience supporting process improvement, system change, testing, automation or wider transformation activity is desirable.

Professional Qualifications and Education

  • No specific degree classification is required. Relevant experience in management information, operational reporting, data analysis, workflow administration, process improvement or transformation will be considered.
  • Relevant training or qualifications in data analysis, Excel, Power BI, business analysis, process improvement or project delivery would be advantageous but are not essential.

Key Competencies

  • Workflow management and tracker governance
  • Data accuracy, controls and attention to detail
  • Planning, prioritisation and delivery against deadlines
  • Problem solving and continuous improvement
  • Stakeholder communication and constructive challenge

title: Curriculum Development Officer – Health Professions Education
description:
About the Project

The Partnership for Education of Health Professionals (PEP) is a multi-country initiative aimed at strengthening institutional capacity for education on cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) across East Africa. Implemented in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and Ethiopia, the programme equips health training institutions with the systems, tools, and competencies needed to develop a health workforce skilled in CMD prevention and care.

In Ethiopia, the project supports CMD integration into pre-service and in-service education, strengthens faculty and preceptor capacity, promotes digital and blended learning and simulation, and supports educational research. Implemented over 36 months in collaboration with government institutions, universities, and professional associations, the initiative focuses on preparing nurses, health officers, and medical doctors to deliver effective CMD services, particularly at the primary health care level.

Job Purpose

The Curriculum Development Officer provides technical and operational support for the review, integration, implementation, and evaluation of competency-based health professions curricula under the PEP project. The role focuses on embedding CMD prevention, screening, diagnosis, management, referral, and follow-up competencies into existing medicine, nursing, and health officer programmes, in line with each cadre’s scope of practice.

Working with the Health Professions Education Specialist, institutional curriculum committees, faculty, clinical preceptors, and subject matter experts, the Officer translates assessment findings into curriculum improvements, aligned teaching resources, and assessment tools. The role supports institutional review and approval, faculty preparation, and monitoring of curriculum delivery and learner competency development.

Position Summary

The position plays a central role in:

  • Mapping existing curricula and identifying CMD competency and content gaps.
  • Integrating measurable learning outcomes into courses, modules, and clinical placements.
  • Aligning teaching methods, learning resources, and assessments with required competencies.
  • Supporting faculty and preceptors to implement and assess revised curricula.
  • Monitoring implementation quality and documenting improvements and lessons.

Key Responsibilities

Programme Implementation and Coordination

  • Translate assigned curriculum activities into practical workplans with clear deliverables, timelines, responsibilities, and review milestones; track progress and escalate delays or resource gaps.
  • Coordinate curriculum reviews, consultations, and validation workshops with partner institutions and project staff; maintain action logs and follow up agreed decisions.
  • Use training and capacity needs assessment findings and institutional evidence to prioritize curriculum strengthening activities and align them with approved PEP workplans.

Curriculum Review and Integration

  • Support systematic review of medicine, nursing, and health officer curricula and map CMD competencies across courses, modules, teaching methods, assessments, and clinical learning experiences.
  • Identify content gaps, duplication, sequencing problems, and differences between the written curriculum and actual delivery; prepare curriculum mapping matrices and actionable recommendations.
  • Support integration of priority CMD competencies into existing curricula without introducing stand-alone courses or additional credit hours unless formally approved by the relevant institutions and authorities.
  • Support the alignment of proposed revisions with national competency frameworks, applicable education and accreditation requirements, current clinical guidance, and cadre-specific scope of practice.
  • Participate in curriculum review workshops, technical working groups and community of practice.
  • Prepare revision packages, change logs, and validation records of the curriculum;
  • Support institutional curriculum committees through review and approval and maintain a record of decisions.

Competency-Based Curriculum Development

  • Work with faculty and subject matter experts to define measurable learning outcomes covering knowledge, clinical and practical skills, communication, and professional attitudes.
  • Support faculty and subject matter experts to align competency and learning outcomes with teaching strategies, practice opportunities, assessment methods, and progression expectations; ensure appropriate sequencing across programme years.
  • Assist faculty and subject matter experts in developing learning modules, study guides, practical exercises, and case-based learning materials that integrates prevention, early detection, risk assessment, patient counselling, referral, and continuity of care alongside disease management, with attention to primary health care realities.
  • Promote integration of patient-centered care, interprofessional learning, evidence use, and appropriate simulation and clinical practice within revised modules.
  • Support incorporation of evidence-based and guideline-driven CMD content.

Assessment Blueprint and Tool Development

  • Support institution in the development of CMD assessment blueprints with faculty and assessment committees under the technical guidance of the Health Professions Education Specialist.
  • Support institutions in the development of matrices linking competencies and learning outcomes to assessment methods, content coverage, cognitive level, weighting, and timing, including knowledge, skills, and professional behaviours.
  • Support development of assessment tools including multiple-choice, short-answer questions, Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) stations, workplace-based assessments, skills checklists, and scoring rubrics.
  • Support assessor orientation, moderation, standard-setting, and review of assessment results to improve validity, reliability, fairness, and consistency; retain institutional authority for assessment approval and progression decisions.
  • Promote timely learner feedback and remediation linked to identified competency gaps, while protecting assessment materials and confidential learner records.
  • Promote use of competency-based assessment approaches across participating programs.

Educational Resource Development and Digital Integration

  • Coordinate development and adaptation of facilitator guides, learner materials, clinical cases, practical exercises, and job aids aligned with approved learning outcomes and CMD guidance.
  • Work with the Online and Blended Learning Officer to translate curriculum requirements into digital and blended learning activities, including links to face-to-face teaching, simulation, and clinical practice.
  • Ensure educational resources are evidence-based, learner-centered, and aligned with competency requirements.
  • Provide curriculum and assessment inputs for innovative methods, including virtual patient cases and AI-assisted resource development; ensure expert review of accuracy, relevance, bias, and alignment before use.
  • Maintain an organized repository of curriculum and assessment resources with references, permissions, version control, review dates, and appropriate access restrictions.

Faculty Engagement and Capacity Building

  • Orient faculty, department heads, and clinical preceptors to curriculum changes, learning outcomes, teaching resources, and assessment requirements.
  • Support practical workshops and coaching on competency-based education, curriculum alignment, case-based teaching, clinical learning, and assessment blueprinting.
  • Facilitate consultations with department heads, curriculum committees, and educators during curriculum implementation.
  • Gather feedback from faculty, preceptors, and learners and support resolution of implementation challenges through agreed institutional channels.

Curriculum Quality Assurance and Implementation

  • Support institutions to develop implementation plans covering teaching schedules, faculty preparation, learning resources, clinical practice opportunities, and assessment arrangements.
  • Support institutions in applying agreed quality assurance criteria to curriculum documents and resources; support review of implementation using teaching plans, course records, assessments, and stakeholder feedback.
  • Monitor whether CMD content and learning activities are delivered as intended; identify gaps in coverage, practice opportunities, and assessment and follow up corrective actions.
  • Contribute to periodic curriculum reviews and improvement cycles, drawing on learner performance and institutional feedback.

Research and Knowledge Management

  • Support education research and evaluations related to curriculum integration, assessment, and implementation in collaboration with research and monitoring staff.
  • Document best practices, challenges, and lessons; contribute to technical briefs, reports, and learning exchanges across partner institutions and PEP country teams.
  • Synthesize relevant evidence for curriculum review and share findings through project learning forums and communities of practice.

Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships

  • Work with the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Education, universities, health science colleges, professional associations, regulatory bodies, and clinical training sites to support coordinated curriculum strengthening.
  • Facilitate technical consultations and validation processes that include curriculum committees, faculty, preceptors, and learner representatives.
  • Promote shared competency expectations across partner institutions while respecting institutional approval processes and programme-specific requirements.

Monitoring Evaluation and Reporting

  • Work with the monitoring, evaluation, and learning team to track curriculum mapping, revisions, approvals, faculty orientation, adoption, and implementation against agreed milestones and indicators.
  • Maintain accurate records and prepare curriculum review reports, workshop summaries, progress updates, and inputs to project and donor reports.
  • Support baseline, midline, and end line assessments of curriculum implementation and competency outcomes, and use findings to recommend improvements.
  • Contribute to project reporting requirements and donor deliverables.

Gender and Inclusion

  • Integrate gender, equity, disability inclusion, and respectful care into learning outcomes, cases, teaching resources, and assessment design.
  • Promote meaningful participation of women and underrepresented groups in curriculum consultations and faculty development activities.
  • Review materials and assessment tools for bias and accessibility barriers, and support fair learning and assessment opportunities across institutional and clinical settings.

Qualifications and Experiences

  • Bachelor’s degree in Medicine, Nursing, Public Health, or another health sciences discipline.
  • Master’s degree in Health Professions Education, Medical Education, Public Health, Curriculum Studies, or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant professional experience in health professions education or curriculum development, including practical involvement in curriculum review and implementation.
  • Demonstrated experience in curriculum mapping, gap analysis, measurable learning outcome development, and competency-based curriculum integration.
  • Experience developing teaching resources and assessment tools; experience in assessment blueprinting, OSCE development, or workplace-based assessment is highly desirable.
  • Experience facilitating faculty workshops and working with universities, health training institutions, curriculum committees, or educational regulatory bodies.
  • Working knowledge of digital and blended learning and the responsible use of AI-assisted educational tools; ability to collaborate with digital learning specialists.
  • Experience in CMD, noncommunicable diseases, primary health care, or health workforce development programmes is an advantage.
  • Strong technical writing, communication, and facilitation skills in English and Amharic.

Core Competencies

Technical Competencies

  • Curriculum development and review
  • Competency-based education
  • Curriculum mapping and gap analysis
  • Assessment blueprint development
  • Educational measurement and evaluation
  • Learning outcome development
  • Instructional design
  • Health professions education
  • CMD/NCD technical knowledge

Professional Competencies

  • Project planning and coordination
  • Technical writing and report preparation
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Workshop facilitation
  • Problem-solving and analytical thinking
  • Attention to detail
  • Quality assurance

Working Conditions

  • Based in Addis Ababa, with regular travel to partner institutions and clinical training sites.
  • Works closely with academic departments, curriculum and assessment committees, government counterparts, and project teams.
  • Requires flexibility to coordinate institutional review cycles, facilitate workshops, and meet project deadlines.

title: Technical Architect
description:

This role is focused on designing and delivering robust, scalable, and secure technical solutions across corporate platforms and customer‑facing services. You will work closely with delivery teams to translate requirements into high‑quality technical architectures that can be built, operated, and supported with confidence.

This is a hands‑on role working closely with delivery teams. Technical Architects at NEC stay closely involved in implementation, providing practical guidance, supporting teams through delivery, and ensuring solutions meet both functional and non‑functional requirements.

The role suits someone who enjoys solving complex technical problems, working across infrastructure and cloud platforms, and collaborating with others to deliver reliable outcomes.

  • Producing technical architecture designs for corporate platforms and customer solutions across on‑premise, data centre, and public cloud environments.

title: Customer Experience Manager
description:
About Zūm:

Zūm is revolutionizing mass mobility with its Connected Mobility Experience (Zūm CMX™) system that connects and coordinates people, vehicles, and operations in real time. In the $50 billion student mobility market – the largest segment of the mass mobility industry – Zūm CMX is transforming a daily source of anxiety and disruption into a reliable, transparent, and efficient mobility experience for students and families. Today, more than 7,500 schools rely on Zūm CMX. Recognized globally for its innovative approach and operational execution, Zūm has been named to Fast Company’s World’s Most Innovative Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50 and Changemakers, the World Economic Forum, and the Financial Times’ Fastest Growing Companies lists. Zūm is backed by leading investors including Sequoia Capital, GIC, TPG, and Softbank.

Who You Are:

Zūm provides safe, reliable, technology-enabled student transportation for school districts. As we launch new districts and deepen existing partnerships, we’re hiring a Customer Experience Manager to own the district relationship once the contract is signed.

You’ll be the day-to-day partner for transportation directors and district leaders in your region. That means working side by side with Operations to deliver on our commitments, staying on every issue until the district confirms it’s resolved, and presenting results to district leadership and boards. You’ll also spot risk early and lead renewal conversations. This is a hands-on role for someone who is organized, responsive, and just as comfortable in the district office as in the yard.

What You'll Do:

  • District partnership: Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for assigned districts, building trusted relationships with transportation directors and district staff.
  • Presentations and reporting: Build and deliver business reviews, launch decks, and board or leadership presentations that clearly communicate performance, progress, and next steps.
  • Execution with Operations: Partner daily with regional Operations and yard leaders to turn district requests and commitments into action and confirm they are completed.
  • Direct follow-up: Own communication back to districts on open issues, service concerns, and requests, with clear timelines, status updates, and closure.
  • Escalations: Identify service gaps early, document them, and route them to Operations, Technology, or Finance. Keep the VP informed on high-risk accounts.
  • Retention: Monitor account health and sentiment, flag churn risk early, and carry out account plans set with the VP.
  • Renewals and growth: Prepare renewal materials and support Ops and Sales on rebids, renewals, and expansion opportunities.
  • Onboarding: Coordinate launch activities for new districts, including readiness checklists, dry runs, and district and family communications.
  • Technology adoption: Train and support district staff and families on the Zūm CMX platform and drive usage.
  • Metrics and reporting: Track health scores and KPIs, including on-time performance, response times, and sentiment, and turn them into weekly action.
  • Voice of customer: Capture district feedback and share recurring themes with Product, Technology, and Operations.

What Success Looks Like:

  • First 30 days: Learn the product, shadow handoffs, and meet your assigned districts and regional Ops leads.
  • First 90 days: Establish strong rapport as district thought partner, run kickoffs or take over existing accounts, with a success plan in place for each district.
  • First year: Hit retention and renewal targets, improve on-time performance and response metrics in your region, and contribute to the CS playbook.

What You Bring To Zūm:

  • 5+ years in customer experience/success, account management, or district-level roles in student transportation, logistics, SaaS, or a similar service-critical field.
  • Strong presentation skills, with experience building and delivering executive-ready materials to district leaders or boards.
  • Proven ability to coordinate with operations teams and drive cross-functional work to completion.
  • Exceptional organization and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple districts and deadlines at once.
  • Fluency with customer data, turned into weekly action.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication.
  • Willingness to travel up to 80% within the region.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
The targeted base salary range for this role is listed in the compensation section below. Actual salary may be above or below this range based on factors such as location, skills, and relevant experience. In addition, this position may include additional compensation in the form of equity or commissions. If you are a full-time salaried or hourly worker, we offer the following benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Holidays, Wellness, Vacation, and more. The targeted pay range for this role in US CA is: $115,000 to $145,000

title: Senior Software Engineer - Robotics
description:
About the role

We’re looking for a strong Senior Software engineer with a passion for robotics to help deliver reliable software for our cell therapy manufacturing platform. You’ll spend your time designing, building, testing and improving software, from interfaces with integrated mobile robots and low-level factory control to factory operation, automation and orchestration.

You’ll work within the robotics team and closely with colleagues across software and systems engineering teams to turn requirements into working solutions. You’ll contribute to technical design and help resolve delivery challenges, while mentoring other engineers and promoting high-quality software.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll regularly deploy software onto physical systems, run integration tests with robots and connected bioprocess equipment, and investigate issues at the boundary between software and hardware. Professional robotics experience is welcome, but is not required: we’re interested in your software engineering skills, curiosity and enthusiasm for learning.

What you’ll do

  • Take technical ownership of the design, architecture, implementation and debugging of maintainable software components, services and interfaces across the robotics platform, driving key architectural decisions and ensuring solutions are scalable, robust and aligned with long-term platform objectives.

  • Integrate software with robots, devices and equipment.

  • Develop and run tests on hardware to verify behaviour, diagnose failures and check fixes under realistic operating conditions.

  • Build quality into delivery through test-driven development, automated testing, continuous integration, and code review.

  • Mentor colleagues, share technical knowledge and help junior engineers deliver consistent, high-quality software.

  • Collaborate across disciplines to resolve integration issues and deliver working features at a sustainable pace.

  • Maintain clear technical documentation and test evidence to support development, verification and regulatory requirements.

What you’ll bring

  • Significant experience delivering complex software, with strong skills in design, implementation, testing and debugging across the development lifecycle.

  • High proficiency in Python programming.

  • Strong understanding of object-oriented programming and software design patterns, with experience building backend services or applications and integrating systems through APIs or messaging.

  • Experience with distributed systems using message-oriented or event-based approaches.

  • Good engineering habits, including version control, automated testing and continuous integration.

  • The ability to mentor other engineers, explain technical ideas clearly and collaborate with colleagues across disciplines.

  • A genuine interest in robotics and the willingness to work hands-on with hardware, learning how to test and troubleshoot integrated systems.

Desirable skills

These are useful additions, rather than requirements. Robotics experience can come from personal projects, study, research or professional work.

  • Robotics or automation experience, including ROS or ROS 2, mobile robots, robotic arms, motion control or machine vision.

  • Experience integrating software with hardware, low-level peripherals or industrial communication protocols such as MQTT.

  • Experience with factory control, automation, orchestration or safety-relevant software.

  • Front-end development, for example using TypeScript or JavaScript with a web framework.

  • Experience with virtualisation, containers, cloud services or IoT integration using GCP, Azure or AWS.

  • Experience developing software in medical or biotechnology settings, including verification, traceability and regulatory documentation.

Cellular Origins is based at Melbourn Science Park, just 10 miles south of Cambridge. Our newly renovated premises offer modern office, laboratory and engineering spaces, surrounded by green spaces. We foster an entrepreneurial and collaborative culture, where ideas are encouraged, innovation thrives, and everyone has the freedom to do their best work.

Our employee benefits include:

  • 25 days holiday
  • Employer pension contribution of 10% of salary
  • Private medical insurance for employees and dependants
  • Subsidised lunches
  • Enhanced family friendly leave
  • Life insurance worth 6x salary
  • Electric car leasing scheme
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Season ticket loan

  • Governance, risk and quality

title: Lead Splunk Engineer
location: Fort Belvoir, VA or Albuquerque, NM
description:
Who we are.

Platinum Technologies is a Northern Virginia based integrated solutions firm that specializes in PaaS, Cybersecurity & AI Platform development for the Defense and Federal Sectors. Our team solves hard problems and helps our Mission Partners achieve their goals. If you are self-motivated, possess demonstrated learning agility, and are passionate about delivering high-quality work products – we want to hear from you.

We lead with technical expertise, but that is just the tip of the iceberg – the ‘Why’ matters. At Platinum, we don’t hire people to just do a job. We provide professional and leadership development to complement our self-motivated domain experts. Our teammates are dot-connecting leaders that operate in a mutually accountable environment to deliver thought leadership, expert technical analysis, and quality execution for our clients.

You.

Platinum Technologies currently has an opportunity for an AIOps Engineer SME to lead the design, deployment, and management of AIOps solutions supporting mission-critical IT operations. This role will transform IT Service Management (ITSM) capabilities through predictive analytics, unified observability, and automated incident response. The engineer will serve as technical lead, coordinating with Network Engineering, ServiceNow, SolarWinds, and cybersecurity teams to strengthen the reliability and security of DoD networks and systems.

This role is located in Fort Belvoir, VA or Albuquerque, NM. Candidate must hold an active Secret clearance at the time of hire. U.S. citizenship is required.

What you get to do.

• Lead the AIOps initiative and coordinate Network Engineering, ServiceNow, and SolarWinds teams to establish unified telemetry pipelines.

• Architect closed-loop remediation workflows integrating Splunk IT Service Intelligence (ITSI) alerts with ServiceNow Event Management and Incident Management.

• Design and sustain Splunk AIOps solutions across classified and unclassified environments for real-time operational visibility.

• Normalize and correlate SolarWinds network performance and fault data with server and application logs to assess enterprise health.

• Build and tune machine learning models using Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK) to identify anomalies, potential cyber threats, and infrastructure degradation.

• Engineer secure telemetry ingestion pipelines from cross-domain solutions and tactical edge devices.

• Use Splunk ITSI to correlate events, reduce alert noise, and prioritize high-impact mission incidents.

• Collaborate with the Cyber Security Service Provider (CSSP) to support defensive cyber operations (DCO).

• Ensure observability solutions comply with applicable DoD STIGs and IL5/IL6 requirements; maintain architecture documentation and compliance traceability.

• Evaluate evolving AIOps capabilities relevant to DoD, federal, and intelligence mission systems.

Required Skills.

• Bachelor’s degree with 12–15 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree with 10–13 years of relevant experience; a technical doctorate or relevant experience, education, and training may be considered in lieu of degree requirements.

• Active Secret security clearance at the time of hire and U.S. citizenship.

• Active DoD IAT Level II certification (e.g., Security+ CE, CySA+, GSEC, or SSCP).

• 7+ years of Splunk Enterprise experience, including architectural design, cluster management, and advanced Search Processing Language (SPL).

• 3+ years implementing AIOps workflows and integrations with enterprise ITSM solutions such as ServiceNow for automated root-cause analysis and remediation.

• Experience developing, testing, and tuning supervised and unsupervised models with Splunk MLTK.

• Advanced scripting and automation experience, including Python, custom search commands, APIs, and remediation workflows.

• Experience leading technical working groups and coordinating infrastructure and development teams.

• Experience in a DoD operations center (NOC/SOC) or supporting mission-critical systems and networks.

• Ability to present technical designs, plans, and analyses of alternatives to technical leadership boards for approval.

Preferred Skills.

• Experience integrating SolarWinds telemetry with Splunk ITSI and ServiceNow Event Management.

• Experience supporting observability and security operations across classified enclaves or cross-domain environments.

The Company is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability, protected veteran status, race, color, religious creed, national origin, citizenship, marital status, sex, sexual orientation/gender identity, age, or genetic information.

title: Head of Platform Engineering
description:
This role is key in an important phase of growth for Cellular Origins, with authority over mission critical decisions and chance to have real organisation impact. Cellular Origins has established an Engineering Department to provide the professional homes in which capability, standards and careers are built. Cross-departmental programmes bring those capabilities together around product developments and customer outcomes. You will own the Platform Engineering capability.

Your mandate spans Engineering strategy and execution: best practice, appropriate process, resources, skills, leadership development and succession. Working alongside those leading Product and Application Development, Customer Delivery and Operations, you will meet urgent programme needs without compromising platform coherence, reliability or scalability.

What you will own

This is a hands-on organisational leadership role. You will get close enough to the work to understand what is really happening, ask incisive questions, resolve ambiguity, remove barriers and make sure decisions turn into action. You will need the breadth and judgement to lead experienced specialists and close cross-disciplinary decisions.

  • Set direction and priorities. Translate company and product strategy into a clear platform-engineering strategy, a prioritised roadmap, and credible investment, capacity and resource choices.
  • Leadership. Lead and develop the team leaders for software, hardware, electronics and firmware, robotics and systems integration. Set clear expectations, establish accountability, give direct feedback and build a strong succession plans.
  • Drive delivery. Make priorities visible, demand realistic plans, use meaningful measures, surface risk early, resolve blockers and intervene decisively where work is drifting.
  • Set engineering standards. Establish and continually improve the practices needed to engineer complex systems well, including architecture, design review, integration, verification and validation, configuration and change control, reliability, maintainability and lifecycle support.
  • Protect and evolve the platform. Assure the coherence of the core technology platform and the quality of major technical decisions. Balance immediate customer needs with reuse, modularity, technical debt, product integrity and long-term scale.
  • Make the matrix work. Partner with the Head of Product and Application Development to turn product and application priorities into executable platform plans; with Customer Delivery leadership on commitments, sequencing and resource trade-offs; and with Operations leadership on design for manufacture, supply, installation, service and support.
  • Represent platform engineering externally. Lead critical technical conversations with customers, partners and suppliers, building confidence through clarity, sound judgement and reliable delivery.
  • Build future capability. Work with others to evolve the department to meet the needs of the business, creating talent plans, skill strategy, professional development, knowledge sharing and succession so the department is ready for the next stage of the business.
  • Leadership. Proven experience leading a substantial multidisciplinary engineering department through senior managers or discipline leaders, with clear evidence of improving delivery and organisational performance through coaching, setting a high bar, handling performance directly, shaping organisations, hiring well and building skills and succession.
  • Relevant system complexity. Experience taking integrated automation, robotics, electromechanical systems or other complex capital equipment from concept through integration, deployment and support.
  • Technical breadth and systems judgement. Credibility across software, embedded systems, electronics, hardware, controls, robotics and integration; able to challenge experts and close cross-disciplinary decisions .
  • A platform mindset. Experience balancing architecture, modularity, reuse, technical debt and lifecycle needs with the immediate demands of products, applications and customer programmes.
  • Engineering rigour. A practical command of quality, safety, design assurance, verification and validation, configuration and change, reliability and continuous improvement.
  • Commercial and customer judgement. The ability to balance scope, cost, resources, timescales and technical risk, and to represent engineering credibly with customers, partners and suppliers.
  • Clear communication and influence. The ability to create alignment across technical and non-technical groups, explain complex choices simply and build confidence with senior stakeholders.
  • Useful context, not a narrow pedigree. Experience in a regulated, safety-critical or high-reliability environment would be valuable. Life sciences or GMP experience is helpful but not essential.

The leadership style we value

You listen widely, then decide. You are direct, fair, calm under pressure and low ego. You stay close enough to delivery to see reality and remove blockers, but you build leaders and systems that do not depend on you for every answer. You are proactive, curious and relentless about follow-through.

Cellular Origins is based at Melbourn Science Park, just 10 miles south of Cambridge. Our newly renovated premises offer modern office, laboratory and engineering spaces, surrounded by green spaces. We foster an entrepreneurial and collaborative culture, where ideas are encouraged, innovation thrives, and everyone has the freedom to do their best work.

  • Private medical insurance for employees and dependants
  • Subsidised lunches
  • Enhanced family friendly leave
  • Life insurance worth 6x salary

We're looking for strong collaborators who deliver exceptional client experiences and thrive in fast-paced, team-oriented environments.   • Experience leading enterprise AI, digital transformation, or platform modernization initiatives within financial services, capital markets, wealth management, or FinTech.

  • Experience across Generative AI, Large Language Models, Agentic AI, machine learning platforms, AI governance, data foundations, and cloud-native technologies.
  • Experience in being able to translate complex business challenges into AI-powered solutions, align senior stakeholders, influence without direct authority, and communicate effectively with executive, board, and technical audiences.

  • Trading and wealth technology modernization
  • Responsible AI, model governance, risk, and compliance
  • Platform architecture, data products, and cloud-native engineering
  • Executive influence, stakeholder alignment, and clear communication

Preferences

  • Experience establishing or scaling an AI Center of Excellence or federated enterprise AI operating model.
  • Experience creating reusable AI platforms, APIs, intelligent workflows, or decision services adopted across multiple business domains.
  • Experience leading modernization of mission-critical, high-volume trading or investment platforms in a complex regulated organization.


Pay Range:

$179,941.00 - $299,833.00


Actual base salary varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location. LPL Financial Holdings Inc. Mission-Driven Problem Solvers – The problems in missile defense demand ingenuity. We want engineers, technicians, and corporate professionals who approach challenges with curiosity, embrace failure as a learning opportunity, and stay focused on delivering the best solution for the mission.

Total Ownership – We seek those who take full responsibility for delivering flight-ready work while recognizing that no one succeeds alone. The best engineers, technicians, and corporate professionals make their teammates better, knowing that complementary skills create force multiplication and drive mission success.


PROGRAM MANAGER


DESCRIPTION

Long Wall is seeking a motivated and technically capable Program Manager to support the execution and growth of programs serving the U.S. Department of War (DoW) and other customers. As a key interface between Long Wall and our customers, you will support program execution, customer engagement, and technical coordination, helping keep programs on schedule, on budget, and aligned with contractual requirements.

You will work closely with Program Management leadership, engineering, contracts, and finance teams, government program offices, and industry partners, turning plans into schedules, tracking commitments through to closure, and ensuring customers receive clear, accurate information about program status. This is a hands-on role in a fast-moving environment and a direct path to building program management expertise. You will gain real experience with defense acquisition, from traditional contracting to newer, faster pathways such as Other Transaction (OT) agreements and rapid prototyping, along with government contracting and customer relationship management.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Represent Long Wall in meetings, technical discussions, program reviews, and coordination activities with U.S. Government customers, and serve as the point of contact for designated program activities
  • Build and maintain professional working relationships with government program managers, contracting personnel, technical representatives, and industry partners
  • Prepare and deliver program briefings, status reports, presentations, and other customer-facing materials, and drive customer action items to closure
  • Support the planning, coordination, and execution of programs from contract award through delivery and closeout, working across engineering, contracts, business functions, subcontractors, and vendors
  • Develop and maintain program schedules, milestones, and performance tracking tools, and track contractual deliverables, including Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) items, to on-time completion
  • Track program budgets, expenditures, and financial performance against plan in coordination with Contracts and Finance
  • Monitor program performance, identify risks, scope changes, and schedule impacts, and recommend corrective actions to Long Wall leadership
  • Support program reviews, technical interchange meetings, milestone reviews, and customer reporting requirements
  • Partner with engineering to understand program technical objectives, support requirements and verification activities, and communicate technical progress, challenges, and proposed solutions to customers
  • Build working knowledge of DoW acquisition processes and FAR/DFARS requirements, and ensure program activities comply with contractual obligations, Long Wall policies, and security and export control requirements

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Science, Systems Engineering, Business Administration, Project Management, or a related discipline
  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience in program management or a similar field

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Genuine interest in building a career in program management, with the drive to learn quickly and take on increasing responsibility
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with close attention to schedules, budgets, contractual commitments, and deliverables
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare and deliver professional presentations
  • Confidence and professionalism when interacting with government officials, military personnel, senior leadership, and technical stakeholders
  • Ability to understand government customer priorities, represent Long Wall effectively, and build trusted, productive relationships with customers and partners
  • Technical aptitude to understand complex technical programs and communicate effectively with engineering teams
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, track commitments, and meet deadlines in a dynamic, fast-moving environment
  • Ownership and follow-through on assigned responsibilities, with sound judgment about which issues need management attention and how to operate within delegated authority
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and Microsoft Project or a comparable scheduling tool
  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of experience in program or project management, project coordination, systems engineering, or business operations, ideally in aerospace and defense (internships, co-ops, and military service count)
  • Experience working with government program offices, military customers, or prime contractors
  • Exposure to DoW acquisition pathways, such as programs of record, Other Transaction (OT) agreements, SBIR/STTR, or rapid prototyping efforts
  • Familiarity with the FAR and DFARS, common contract types (e.g., firm-fixed-price, cost-plus), and contract deliverables such as CDRLs
  • Experience building or maintaining integrated master schedules (IMS), or familiarity with earned value management (EVM) concepts
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance (Secret or above)
  • CAPM or PMP certification, or progress toward one
  • Experience in a startup or fast-growing aerospace, defense, or hardware environment

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time
  • Ability to use a computer to complete assignments
  • Ability to communicate with individuals and groups in person, by phone, and via telepresence
  • Ability to pick up to 12lbs
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee will typically work in an office environment
  • Ability to travel periodically to customer sites, government facilities, partner locations, and between Long Wall sites as required
ITAR Requirement
This position requires access to information protected under US export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and/or the Export Administration Regulations. As such, US person status (including US citizens, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted U.S. asylum status, or individuals admitted in U.S. refugee status) is a required qualification for this position.
Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, genetics, or citizenship status (when otherwise legally authorized to work and access export-controlled data) and will not be discriminated against on the basis of such characteristics or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. We encourage applicants of all ages.
National Security Suitability
Depending on the position, Long Wall may require the successful completion of a national security suitability screening in addition to its standard background check. Where required, the screening is conducted by Long Wall’s Facility Security Officer following offer acceptance and may include verification of any current or prior U.S. government security clearances or public trust positions. Information provided during the screening is used solely to determine suitability for the role and is held in confidence by Security. title: Battery Test Engineer - Aeromechanical
description:
Pivotal is the leader in the emerging market of electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft. We design, develop, and manufacture light eVTOL aircraft and are renowned for the BlackFly aircraft the world's first light eVTOL to fly manned missions and enter the consumer market.
Efficient, compact, and simple, Pivotal aircraft are designed for a wide range of consumer, public service, and defense applications. Our distinctive tilt-aircraft architecture and scalable platform have been flying for over 10 years. Last year we announced our next-generation aircraft, the Helix, which is rapidly progressing toward general release and scalable production in 2026.
Mobility is one of the most highly-valued areas of modern technology investments. This is the right company, in the right space, the right strategy, at the right time. If you are ready for adventure, we invite you to join our amazing team and grow with us.

About the Job

The Battery Engineering team at Pivotal is seeking a hands-on Battery Test Engineer to own the design and execution of battery performance characterization, thermal-runaway, abuse, environmental, and durability testing. This engineer will translate system risks and requirements into safe, instrumented, repeatable tests at the cell and pack levels, then convert test results into defensible engineering evidence and actionable design improvements.

Responsibilities

  • Own test planning and hands-on execution for lithium-ion cells and aircraft battery packs.

  • Plan and execute electrical and thermal performance characterization of cell candidates and prototype packs, including capacity, DCIR, power capability, mission-profile cycling, and thermal response across temperature.

  • Operate high-power battery cyclers, cell cyclers, and environmental chambers, and maintain test profiles, data pipelines, and test-article configuration records.

  • Deliver correlation-ready datasets to the simulation team and support model-versus-test comparison.

  • Design, build, and execute thermal-runaway initiation, propagation, containment, venting, and mitigation tests, including fabrication of test articles, trigger methods, fixtures, and instrumentation appropriate to test objectives.

  • Develop environmental and durability tests covering temperature, thermal cycling, altitude or low-pressure exposure, humidity, vibration, mechanical shock, and transportation conditions as applicable.

  • Define test objectives, hazards, instrumentation needs, data-acquisition architecture, trigger logic, sampling rates, acceptance criteria, and stop conditions.

  • Prepare test articles, fixtures, chambers, power equipment, cooling systems, sensors, high-speed video, thermal imaging, and data-acquisition systems.

  • Lead test readiness reviews, job-hazard analyses, emergency planning, exclusion-zone definition, and coordination with EHS, facilities, fire-safety, and external laboratories.

  • Execute testing safely, monitor tests in real time, respond to anomalies, and protect personnel, facilities, test assets, and data integrity.

  • Analyze temperature, voltage, current, pressure, gas, flame, ejecta, and propagation behavior, as applicable to the test objective and facility capability.

  • Author clear test plans, procedures, reports, nonconformance records, root-cause assessments, and design recommendations.

  • Support model correlation and work with design engineers to improve containment, cooling, sensing, venting, and protection strategies.

  • Manage external test laboratories, including statement-of-work development, setup reviews, witnessing, data acceptance, and issue resolution.

  • Maintain calibrated instrumentation, safe lab practices, test configuration control, data traceability, and lessons learned.

  • Support transportation and environmental compliance test programs, including UN 38.3 activities, when applicable to the product and program phase.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Electrical, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical field.

  • Three or more years of hands-on battery, environmental, abuse, reliability, or aerospace hardware testing experience.

  • Experience designing instrumented tests and selecting thermocouples, voltage and current measurement, pressure sensing, thermal imaging, and data-acquisition hardware.

  • Working knowledge of lithium-ion battery hazards, high-voltage safety, stored-energy hazards, fire risk, and safe test operations.

  • Experience developing test fixtures, procedures, hazard controls, and technical reports.

  • Ability to troubleshoot hardware, instrumentation, wiring, communications, and data-quality issues in the laboratory.

  • Ability to work on-site and safely support physically hands-on test setup and execution.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience conducting or witnessing battery thermal-runaway, propagation, overcharge, external heating, short-circuit, crush, or penetration testing.

  • Experience with environmental chambers, vibration systems, thermal cycling, altitude chambers, shock testing, and high-power battery pack cyclers (e.g., Chroma, etc.) or cell cyclers (e.g., Biologic, Arbin).

  • Experience with electric aircraft, EV, UAV, aerospace, defense, or other safety-critical energy systems.

  • Familiarity with UN 38.3 and relevant battery or aerospace environmental-test standards, with the judgment to confirm applicability before defining a compliance plan.

  • Experience with LabVIEW, Python, MATLAB, Dewesoft, NI hardware, or comparable data-acquisition and analysis environments.

  • Experience with fire-safe test cells, exhaust and gas handling, remote monitoring, blast or fragment protection, and emergency-response coordination.

  • Experience managing outside laboratories and reviewing supplier test evidence.

Ideal Candidate

  • Has a strong laboratory and test-floor mindset and takes personal ownership of safe execution and high-quality data.

  • Balances urgency with disciplined readiness reviews, hazard controls, and configuration management.

  • Can move from requirement or failure concern to a practical test method, fixture, procedure, and evidence package.

  • Communicates unexpected results quickly and objectively and helps the team turn failures into design learning.

Attributes Aligned with Our Core Values

  • Safety Above All: Demonstrates a proactive safety mindset by embedding safety into daily work, identifying and mitigating risks, encouraging open dialogue about safety concerns, and continuously improving practices and protocols.
  • Customer Focus: Puts customers at the center of every action by understanding their challenges, delivering meaningful value, and supporting their success.
  • Work Better Together: Seeks and values diverse perspectives, builds cross-functional relationships, and fosters trust through empathetic, fact-based communication and commitment to shared decisions.
  • Be the Pilot: Drives results with clarity and purpose by focusing on what matters most, adapting to change, taking initiative, and owning outcomes.
  • Embrace the Unknown: Navigates ambiguity with resilience and bold thinking, challenges the status quo, and combines innovative ideas with practical approaches to overcome obstacles and drive progress.
  • Respect for People: Fosters a high-performance culture grounded in respect, professionalism, and support by balancing high expectations with a healthy, collaborative environment and being a trusted, dependable teammate.
Applicants must be eligible for employment in the United States and willing to work onsite at our HQ office in Palo Alto, CA.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
description:
Position Summary

At Odyssey, our Cybersecurity Analysts protect our systems, data, and people from evolving cyber threats across cloud and on premises environments. You will monitor and triage alerts from SIEM, EDR, and intrusion detection tools, investigate confirmed threats, and contain incidents by isolating hosts, blocking malicious activity, and escalating as needed. You will document findings, refine detection rules, and partner with IT, engineering, and compliance teams to identify vulnerabilities and drive remediation. You will also support our GRC program by maintaining System Security Plans (SSPs) and POA&Ms, providing audit and assessment evidence, and supporting continuous monitoring aligned with NIST RMF and FedRAMP requirements.

Responsibilities

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Monitors and responds to alerts from tools such as SIEM (Security Information and Event Management), EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response), and intrusion detection systems, then triages each alert to determine whether it is a real threat or a false positive and how urgently it needs attention.
  • For genuine threats, they investigate logs, network traffic, and endpoint activity to understand what happened and how far it spread, then contain the threat by isolating hosts, blocking IPs or accounts, and escalating serious incidents.
  • They document their findings and actions in tickets and incident reports, and they continually refine detection rules to reduce noise and catch new attack techniques.
  • Support NIST SP 800 171, NIST SP 800 53 and CMMC Level 2 requirements and writing control narratives, SSPs, POA&Ms and assessment evidence.

Qualifications

Citizenship: Must be a U.S. citizen

Minimum Required Qualifications

  • Clearance: Eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in information security, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • Years of Experience: 3 to 5 years in security compliance, audit, or GRC, including hands on experience with NIST SP 800-171 or NIST SP 800-53
  • Certifications: CompTIA Security Plus or equivalent

Preferred Qualifications

  • Clearance: Active Secret clearance
  • Years of Experience: 5 to 8 years experience supporting a DoD contractor or SOC organization, including CUI environments (i.e. Microsoft GCC High); prior participation in a C3PAO assessment
  • Certifications: SecurityX Plus, CISA, CRISC, or CISSP

Technical Skills

  • Microsoft 365 and Azure compliance tooling (Purview, Compliance Manager, Defender for Cloud, Intune)
  • SIEM, EDR, and vulnerability scanning tools to support continuous monitoring
  • Security awareness and phishing simulation platforms
  • NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-171A, NIST SP 800-53, and CMMC Level 2 requirements
  • CUI and FCI scoping, asset categorization, and assessment boundary definition
  • Writing control narratives, SSPs, POA&Ms, and assessment evidence package

Interpersonal Skills

  • Serves as primary contact for assessors, prime contractors, and customers
  • Coordinates evidence across HR, facilities, export compliance, and IT
  • Prepares clear, defensible packages for executive signature
  • Holds control owners accountable for findings through closure
  • Communicates compliance status and risk to technical and nontechnical stakeholders

Additional Information

  • Location: Colorado Springs, CO
  • Travel: 5-10%
  • Work Arrangement: Remote or Hybrid (Periodic on location work as needed)

#LI-MP1

Company Overview

Odyssey is a world-class technical, engineering, and integration company serving the warfighting ecosystem with airborne integration, ISR, C2, and warfighter readiness capabilities. Odyssey meets the military’s operational needs by integrating layered defense systems from equipment, technology, and services to data, information, and business operations. We streamline defense acquisition and sustainment, engineering the technical battlefield with domain-specific proficiency to ensure lethality. Odyssey is dedicated to excellent contract execution, peak organizational performance, and fostering a workplace built on employee care.

Odyssey is proud to live out our core values of commitment, ambition, and respect in our work and communities through OdysseyCares, a philanthropic group focused on giving back through direct donations, an employer match program, and volunteering events.

title: Associate Director - Mass Spec Production
description:
Performing critical work that impacts our industry and our world’s health while problem solving and innovating in the field – that is what an Associate Director at KCAS Bio get to do every day. If that gets you excited too, then maybe working as an Associate Director at KCAS Bio is the role for you.

When you work as an Associate Director in the Mass Spectrometry Bioanalysis Production group at KCAS, you get to further our mission by providing operational and scientific leadership across the MSB Production organization. You will lead teams responsible for the execution of regulated bioanalytical studies while driving process harmonization, operational efficiency, quality, capacity, and continuous improvement across the group.

Our Mass Spec Bioanalysis Development team uses LC-MS/MS (Liquid Chromatography–Tandem Mass Spectrometry) techniques and sophisticated sample preparation methods to meet bioanalytical needs for drug discovery, preclinical, and clinical studies, including the bioanalysis of drugs and metabolites, biomarkers, and active endogenous compounds in biological fluids and tissues.

In this role, we will rely on you to:

  • Lead, develop, and coach scientific staff while establishing clear expectations, strengthening team capabilities, and building accountability for performance, quality, and delivery

  • Drive process harmonization and standardization across teams, studies, and workflows while maintaining scientific quality, data integrity, and GLP compliance

  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve laboratory operations through automation, technology, standardized tools, training, and continuous improvement initiatives

  • Perform all aspects of the job in a way that supports company brand and supports company mission, vision, and values

To qualify specifically for this role, you will have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biochemistry, or a related scientific field with at least 7 years of experience in a bioanalytical laboratory environment; advanced degree preferred
  • Strong knowledge of quantitative LC-MS/MS bioanalysis, including bioanalytical sample preparation, instrumentation, data workflows, and regulated study execution
  • Extensive experience working in a GLP/GxP-regulated laboratory environment
  • Demonstrated leadership experience within a scientific or laboratory organization, including developing teams, managing performance, and establishing accountability
  • Demonstrated experience improving laboratory operations, workflows, processes, or productivity within a scientific environment
  • Experience identifying operational bottlenecks, conducting root-cause analysis, and implementing sustainable process improvements

  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills

Our benefits include, and extend beyond, the traditional package. At KCAS Bio, you will enjoy company sponsored events like food trucks, family days and spirit days.
