title: Director, Payment Partnerships
location: San Jose, California, United States of America
description:
The Company

PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.

We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. title: Manager, Product Integrity — Connected Products
description:
Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team. Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.

The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.

We are looking for a leader who can spearhead the product quality and integrity function covering test definition, systems integration, test execution, and holding a high product integrity bar. This leader will lead a hardware testing team. The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.

Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations. Remote days are Monday and Friday.

What you will own

  • The Product Integrity team. Lead a team of test engineers covering production and 100% test, hardware test, reliability test, quality inspection, and overall confirmation of product requirements. You set the direction and the standard; the team executes.
  • Requirements into tests. Turn every hardware requirement in the PRD — from Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance — into a testable requirement with a method, a sample size, an acceptance criterion, and a gate. Product defines the design envelope; you define how we test to it.
  • Gate evidence. Every stage gate (EVT, DVT, PVT) carries your evidence package: what was tested, against which requirement, with what result.
  • Reliability. Define the reliability test plan for each program and own the statistics behind it: sample sizes, confidence levels, and acceleration factors for environmental testing.
  • Production test. Develop fixtures and test software that meet approved cycle times, with test limits tied to expected field performance.
  • Field performance. Review returns and field data, and feed what you learn back into requirements and test plans.

The team and the logistics

  • Team: test engineers covering production test, hardware test, reliability test, and quality inspection. The lab is in North Olmsted.
  • Location: North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA. If based in San Francisco, expect occasional travel to North Olmsted.
  • Travel: ~15%. Travel to factories in Nogales and Tecate, Mexico; Hanoi, Vietnam; and between North Olmsted and San Francisco.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years on connected consumer hardware spanning electrical, mechanical, and firmware.
  • Experience developing factory test fixtures at both board level and end of line.
  • Experience writing requirements and V&V plans.
  • Reliability engineering fluency: accelerated life testing, Weibull and AFR math, sample sizing at a stated confidence, HALT/HASS, thermal, drop, and cycle life. You can design a plan and read a failure.
  • Production test experience: fixtures, test software, DFT, cycle time, and yield at a contract manufacturer.
  • Has led a small technical team and is comfortable setting direction for test engineers who are more hands-on than you.

Nice to have

  • Battery power model development.
  • Sensor products with calibration and drift requirements.
  • Sealed or outdoor enclosures.
  • RF performance characterization.
  • Certification literacy across safety (UL), RF (FCC), and interop (Matter/CSA); NSF/IAPMO for water products or BHMA for locks.

title: Quality Control Associate - Environmental Monitoring
description:
Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing transformative cell and exosome-based therapies for rare diseases. At the forefront of our innovation is Deramiocel (CAP-1002), our lead cell therapy in late-stage development for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. We are also harnessing our proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform to unlock new possibilities in targeted delivery and vaccinology. Every program reflects our commitment to pushing the boundaries of science and delivering life-changing treatments to patients and families who need them most.

The Quality Control Associate for Environmental Monitoring (EM) plays a critical role in maintaining the environmental conditions required for GMP manufacturing. This position is responsible for performing routine and specialized sampling, analyzing trends, documenting results, and ensuring controlled areas maintain compliance with regulatory and internal quality standards. As part of the QC EM team, you will perform hands-on monitoring of air, surfaces, and personnel, as well as water system and utility testing to ensure facility integrity. You will be responsible for maintaining accurate, real-time documentation and supporting investigations into any environmental excursions or anomalies. Working closely with QC, QA, and Production, this role ensures that manufacturing and testing environments remain in a constant state of control to support the production of high-quality therapeutic products.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct routine environmental monitoring in controlled and classified areas in alignment with GMP, ISO, and regulatory requirements.
  • Perform sampling of air, surfaces, water, and equipment using approved methods.
  • Document sampling activities and results accurately in accordance with GMP and data integrity standards.
  • Analyze environmental monitoring data to identify trends, excursions, and required corrective or preventive actions.
  • Escalate atypical results promptly and support the investigation, documentation, and closure of deviations and CAPAs.
  • Maintain calibration, readiness, and routine upkeep of environmental monitoring equipment.
  • Support audit and inspection readiness through compliant documentation and area oversight.
  • Collaborate with QC, QA, and Production to address findings, implement improvements, and maintain a state of control.
  • Follow gowning and cleanroom entry procedures consistently and perform duties in full cleanroom attire.
  • Participate in continual learning, safety programs, and ongoing process improvements.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Chemistry, Microbiology, or a related field.
  • 2–5 years of experience in environmental monitoring or quality control within a regulated environment (pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, or similar).
  • Knowledge of GMP, ISO, FDA expectations, and environmental monitoring standards.
  • Experience performing environmental sampling and handling EM equipment.
  • Strong documentation, data integrity, and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in controlled environments, including cleanrooms.
  • Strong organizational and time‑management skills for handling multiple priorities.

Preferred Qualifications (Nice‑to‑Haves)

  • Experience with viable and non‑viable particle monitoring, active air sampling, and cleanroom incubation workflows.
  • Familiarity with LIMS or other laboratory information systems.
  • Experience supporting audits, inspections, or EM program review.
  • Strong communication and cross‑functional collaboration skills.
  • Experience with troubleshooting trends or environmental anomalies.

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Significant time spent in GMP cleanrooms, including full gowning.
  • Prolonged standing during sampling activities and extended computer use for documentation and trending.
  • May require lifting of equipment or materials up to 20 pounds.
  • Ability to work within laboratory, cleanroom, and manufacturing environments as part of routine monitoring.

Shift/Schedule

  • This position follows a swing shift schedule to support operational needs.
Schedule Details:
  • Primary shift options:Sunday through Thursday | Tuesday through Saturday
  • Typical hours: 12:00 PM to 9:00 PM (may vary based on business needs)
  • Flexibility is required, and occasional adjustments to shift times or days may be necessary.
  • We will confirm your assigned shift prior to your start date.

Why Capricor?

Capricor Therapeutics is advancing cell and exosome-based therapies with a focus on serious diseases where patients and families need new treatment options. Our work is grounded in scientific rigor, collaboration, and a shared commitment to moving meaningful therapies forward. Joining Capricor means being part of a mission-driven team working at the intersection of innovation, execution, and patient impact.

Come Work With Us

At Capricor, you’ll join a collaborative environment where employees are encouraged to contribute, grow, and help build the systems, science, and operations needed to support our next stage of growth. We value people who are thoughtful, accountable, hands-on, and motivated by work that can make a real difference.

Recruiting Fraud Notice

Capricor does not use Skype for interviews or recruiting activities. Candidates will only be contacted by someone using an official Capricor email address ending in @capricor.com. Capricor will never ask candidates to send money, deposit a check, purchase equipment, or provide payment for any reason as part of the recruiting or onboarding process.

Notice to Recruiting Agencies

Capricor Therapeutics does not accept candidate submissions or referrals from recruiting agencies, staffing firms, or third-party recruiters without express written approval from Talent Acquisition and a fully executed agreement with Capricor. Agencies that contact hiring managers directly, solicit business, or submit candidates without prior approval will not be considered for engagement. Any unsolicited submissions will become the property of Capricor Therapeutics, and no fees will be paid for candidates hired as a result of such submissions. We appreciate your cooperation and respect for this policy.

title: Network Infrastructure Engineer
description:
About the role

As a Network Infrastructure Engineer, you’ll be responsible for designing, building and maintaining the compute and network infrastructure in our on-site test environments and remote customer deployments. You will work across a wide range of technologies including server racks, segregated factory networks, industrial workstation connections and remote monitoring.

This is a practical, hands-on role. As well as working with suppliers to specify the appropriate equipment, you’ll build server racks, perform software installation, fit cabling, configure network routing and set up service monitoring.

Working closely with our Platform Engineers, you’ll work with a variety of technical teams to set up network infrastructure for prototype test rigs, demonstration factory lines as well as deploying the finalized designs at customer sites. You’ll be a subject matter expert in correctly selecting and scaling infrastructure to meet the requirements of each type of installation.

This is an opportunity to join a truly multi-disciplinary team and broaden your skillset. As well as working within an established group, you’ll regularly collaborate across robotics, systems engineering and test teams.

What you’ll bring

You’ll have a strong background in the design, implementation and deployment of platform infrastructure in both in-house and remote environments. Your open and collaborative working style combined with a breadth of technical knowledge will allow you to work effectively with the whole team.

Essential:

  • Ability to build and configure server racks, install and connect switches/routers, patch panels and power systems.

  • Ability to appropriately set up and configure networks including considerations of TCP/IP addressing schemes, physical/logical network segmentation, routing and firewall rules.

  • Ability to set up Linux and Windows operating systems and configure remote deployment tools onto bare-metal industrial and embedded PCs.

  • Proactive approach to customer support and system maintenance: clear, early communication to relevant stakeholders that identifies required equipment, reconfiguration, repairs and emerging risks.

Desirable:

  • Interest or previous experience working with robotic automation systems, industrial/embedded PCs or installation in factory environments. Previous experience with Ubiquiti equipment would also be desirable.

  • Experience monitoring the health and capacity of network and compute to ensure reliable factory operation. Ability to diagnose common faults including hardware failures, incorrect configuration and capacity limitations.

  • Experience maintaining and updating network architecture, server racking, cabling and wiring documentation and diagrams.

  • Experiencing selecting and procuring appropriate server hardware, network switches/routers, cabling and UPS systems for a variety of different projects.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Degree or vocational qualification in Computer Engineering, Networking, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field or equivalent industry experience.

title: UX Researcher
description:
OUR STORY:
🇪🇺 Join Scaleway and shape the sovereign cloud of tomorrow !
Since 1999, we have been designing secure, sustainable infrastructures aimed at supporting the most ambitious companies.
Historically known for our dedicated servers (Dedibox), we made a strategic shift to cloud computing in 2015. Staying true to our principles of simplicity, flexibility, and technical excellence, we have become one of the leading players in Europe in the sector.
With the rise of artificial intelligence, we have strengthened our commitment, supported by the Iliad Group, which is investing €3 billion to develop a serious, sovereign AI alternative to American and Asian giants.
Every day, thanks to our fast-growing portfolio of cloud and AI products (bare metal, containerization, serverless, AI, etc.), Scaleway proudly serves thousands of customer across the private and public sector, from corporations like France Télévisions or Hachette Livre, to fast-growing startups like Photoroom and Biolevate, to institutions like the City of Copenhagen.
📍 Our offices are located in Paris, Lille, Toulouse, Rennes, Rouen, Bordeaux and Lyon.

WHY WE NEED YOU ?

Our growth is driving us to strengthen our UX Research team within the Product & Design department to scale our research capabilities and better support product decisions across our core cloud infrastructure.

Your mission will be to lead impactful user research on highly technical products, while developing scalable ResearchOps practices and empowering product teams to conduct research independently, in order to embed user insights into product strategy and continuously improve the experience of our cloud infrastructure users.

YOUR FUTURE TEAM

We work in a collaborative and international environment where the diversity of Scalers, combined with a spirit of sharing, helps bring new projects to life every day, advancing our ambitions together.

You will join a growing team of 2 UX Researchers, within the Design department, working closely with Product Managers and Product Designers across different tribes.

The team focuses on making user research more continuous, accessible and impactful across Scaleway's product organization. Key initiatives include scaling ResearchOps, developing our Insight Hub, enabling People Who Do Research (PwDR), and responsibly integrating AI into research workflows.

You will also collaborate with Solution Architects, Customer Success and Marketing teams when relevant, gaining exposure to a wide range of technical products and customer needs.

YOUR DAILY ROUTINE

  • Lead end-to-end UX research initiatives, from discovery to usability testing and continuous research, focusing on cloud infrastructure products and technical users such as developers, DevOps engineers and system administrators.

  • Partner closely with Product Managers and Product Designers to identify research opportunities, frame relevant research questions and translate findings into actionable product recommendations.

  • Collaborate with Product Designers to make highly technical concepts (e.g. provisioning, networking, storage configuration) understandable and usable, helping Scaleway stand out for usability in a historically technical industry.

  • Develop and scale ResearchOps practices, including research workflows, methodologies, templates and insight management processes.

  • Contribute to the development and adoption of the Insight Hub, ensuring research findings are accessible, reusable and actionable across multiple product tribes.

  • Empower Product Managers, Product Designers and other PwDRs to conduct high-quality research independently through coaching, training and practical research guidelines.

  • Explore and integrate AI-powered tools and automated workflows to improve research efficiency while maintaining methodological rigor and responsible practices.

  • Identify cross-product user needs and behavioral patterns to generate insights that extend beyond individual features or product teams.

  • Advocate for user-centered decision-making, communicate research findings effectively and follow up on their impact on product roadmaps and strategic priorities.

ABOUT YOU

HARDSKILLS :

  • UX Research expertise: 4+ years of experience in UX Research, or UX Design with a strong research focus, including discovery research, usability testing, quantitative and qualitative research methodologies.

  • Technical product experience: Proven experience researching complex B2B products, ideally in cloud infrastructure, developer tools, SaaS or enterprise technology, with the ability to understand technical users and unfamiliar technical concepts.

  • ResearchOps & continuous research: Experience structuring scalable research processes, managing research insights and repositories, and contributing to continuous or always-on research practices.

  • Research enablement & stakeholder collaboration: Experience coaching non-researchers, particularly Product Managers and Product Designers, and translating findings into actionable product decisions within Lean/Agile environments.

  • Research tools & AI: Proficiency with tools such as Figma, FigJam and web/product analytics platforms, with an interest in leveraging AI and automation to improve research workflows and insight management.

  • Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken.

SOFTSKILLS :

  • Proactivity and ownership: You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement and confidently drive research projects forward.

  • Empathy and collaboration: You build strong relationships with stakeholders, understand their constraints and adapt your approach to facilitate effective collaboration.

  • Rigor and pragmatism: You balance methodological quality with business realities, ensuring research remains efficient, relevant and actionable.

  • Curiosity and adaptability: You enjoy learning about unfamiliar technical topics, navigating complexity and continuously developing your expertise.

  • Resilience and positive mindset: You remain engaged and constructive in environments where research impact may take time to materialize, while confidently advocating for the user perspective.

WHAT YOU WILL FIND AT SCALEWAY ++++

Hybrid work: We offer up to 3 days of remote work per week.

Offices: Our offices are spacious, dynamic workspaces with bold design, conveniently located near public transport. Most of our offices feature outdoor spaces (terraces) and bike parking facilities.

Dining: Our chef provides a healthy meal service at the headquarters, and breakfast is available across all our sites year-round. Scalers working from regional sites enjoy a Swile card for lunches.

Well-being commitments: Whether it’s access to a gym, daycare places, or discounted services for caring services, Scaleway is committed to supporting Scalers in maintaining a balanced life.

International environment: With dozens of nationalities, Scaleway offers a stimulating environment where English is as widely spoken as French.

Career & Mobility: Our managers value internal mobility, and opportunities to transition to other entities within the Iliad Group are accessible to all Scalers.

🚀Why join the Scaleway adventure ?

✔ A rich and diverse product offering: Scaleway offers over 100 public cloud products in IaaS, PaaS, and AI.

✔ A cutting-edge technical environment: Scaleway provides modern infrastructures, including high-performance bare metal servers, to tackle exciting technical challenges.

✔ Commitment to responsible cloud: Scaleway is dedicated to a more responsible cloud, with data centers powered solely by renewable energy since 2017, minimizing our ecological footprint and holding top-level certification.

🔜 THE NEXT STEPS …

  • Screening call with HR to discuss your background, motivations and expectations
  • Interview with UX Research Lead, to understand your technical skills and approach to the role
  • Technical interview with the UX Research team and Head of Product, including the presentation of a UX research case study and Q&A, to validate your expertise
  • Culture & fit interview VP of Product Experience & Design, to deepen your discussions
Scaleway is a company certified under SecNumCloud. A background check is mandatory in order to join the company.
At Scaleway, we are committed to building an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has a fair opportunity to thrive.
All applications are considered with care, regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, ethnic or social background, religion, disability, or any other characteristic.
We believe great ideas come from everywhere, and everyone which is why you should definitely apply.

title: Cloud Engineer
description:
The Role

Fastmarkets is seeking a Cloud Engineer to join our worldwide Cloud Engineering team. The team builds the secure, performant and scalable cloud and infrastructure platforms predominantly Azure that our customer-facing products and internal applications run on.

Reporting to the Cloud Lead, you will design, build and maintain that infrastructure as code, deliver secure integrations, and modernise how we build and deploy. This is a hands-on engineering role: everything is infrastructure as code, secure by design, and built with cost, operability and supportability in mind.

You will work closely with Engineering, Data, InfoSec and IT Operations teams, and be expected to bring sound technical judgement able to steer requests towards the right architecture, not just deliver what was asked for.

Principal Accountabilities

  • Infrastructure as Code — design and maintain Terraform for Azure; build plan-only CI, remote state, resource import and reusable modules.
  • CI/CD & DevOps — build GitHub Actions pipelines and migrate legacy CI/CD (TeamCity, Octopus Deploy) onto modern workflows.
  • Containers & deployment — containerise and deploy applications to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) using Docker, Kustomize, ArgoCD (GitOps), Sealed Secrets and Traefik ingress.
  • Secure integrations — deliver integrations between external services and Azure using managed identities, service principals and scoped RBAC.
  • Security & governance — perform security discovery and audits, drive zero-trust and credential-lockdown work, and take designs through security review gates.
  • Documentation & enablement — produce inventories, architecture docs, runbooks and reusable patterns and templates the wider team can adopt.

We recruit talented, dynamic people with diverse backgrounds and experiences, all united by a belief in our mission to provide the world’s leading and most trusted price reporting, events, and intelligence service for the markets we serve. We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a fully inclusive workplace, where everyone feels able to participate and contribute meaningfully.

If you are open-minded, curious, resilient, solutions-oriented and committed to promoting equality, then read on.

KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

We are looking for an individual who is highly motivated, driven, and have a passion to be part of a fast-paced, successful team. Being a strong team player is also important as well as someone who is happy to work flexibly.

Essential

  • 2–4 years in Cloud Engineering, DevOps, platform engineering or infrastructure roles, building and changing production systems in Azure.
  • Microsoft Azure — Resource Groups, Virtual Networks/Subnets, Storage Accounts, Azure SQL, Key Vault, Application Gateway, VMs/VMSS, NSGs.
  • Azure networking & Private Link — Private Endpoints, Private DNS Zones, VNet links, storage firewalls and IP allowlisting, locking down public network access.
  • Terraform — plan/apply workflows, remote state, import blocks, modules, for_each with data-driven tfvars, lifecycle rules, per-environment configuration.
  • GitHub Actions — Terraform plan/apply with approval gates, build/test/deploy pipelines, Git branching and PR review.
  • Containers & Kubernetes — Docker (digest-pinned images, non-root containers), AKS, and core Kubernetes primitives (Deployments, Services, NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota, ConfigMaps/Secrets).
  • Scripting — Python, PowerShell and Bash for automation; comfortable with HCL and YAML.
  • Identity & security — Microsoft Entra ID (service principals, group-based access), least-privilege Azure RBAC, secrets management (Key Vault, GitHub Secrets), and zero-trust principles.
  • Production troubleshooting — structured root-cause analysis under pressure; able to tell expected behaviour from genuine misconfiguration.
  • Risk awareness — sequences privileged changes safely, builds security gates into plans early, and rehearses changes outside production first.
  • Documentation discipline and a standardisation mindset — turns one-off solutions into reusable patterns.

Desirable

  • Migrating legacy build systems (TeamCity, Octopus Deploy; .NET, C++, Delphi toolchains) onto GitHub Actions.
  • GitOps with ArgoCD, Kustomize and Helm; Kubernetes add-ons such as KEDA, Traefik and Sealed Secrets; Azure Container Registry.
  • Configuration management with Ansible.
  • Building internal developer-platform or self-service deployment tooling.
  • Building internal apps and APIs with Python (Flask, FastAPI).
  • Using AI/LLM APIs (e.g. Anthropic Claude, Azure OpenAI) to speed up engineering work.
  • Exposure to Snowflake or other cloud data platforms.

If you're excited about the role but your experience, skills or qualifications don't perfectly align, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Our Values

Fastmarkets people come from all different walks of life. It’s this mix of brilliant personalities, experiences and insights that gives us that warm, open, and friendly culture you can feel as soon as you meet us. But however wonderfully different we all are, there are six things we all have in common – and they form our Fastmarkets values.

Created by our own employees to reflect some of the personal traits that Fastmarkets people have, our values are key to what makes our culture unique. They reflect who each of us are and they're embedded in everything we do. Our values are:

  • METRICS DRIVEN. We use insights to improve our customers’ experience and our business performance
  • ACCOUNTABLE. We are accountable to ourselves and those we work with: we keep our promises and get things done
  • GROWTH MINDSET. This value enables us to be nimble to the changing realities and operate with a sense of urgency
  • INCLUSIVE. We are inclusive and respectful, celebrating each of us and giving everyone a deep sense of belonging with the desire to bring their best self to work every day.
  • CUSTOMER CENTRIC. We are customer-centric in all that we do
  • COLLABORATIVE. We are collaborative, able to work across teams and capitalise on the diversity of intellect, perspectives, and experiences.

We are committed to ensuring all candidates feel welcomed and supported. Should your application advance and you require accommodations for the interview process, please inform us so we can make the necessary arrangements.

Reward and benefits at Fastmarkets

We believe in fair pay and benefits that support you both inside and outside of work. Through Fastmarkets Rewards, you'll have access to a range of core benefits and a flexible allowance, giving you the freedom to tailor your package to suit your lifestyle, wellbeing and financial priorities. We know that everyone's needs are different, so we've designed our benefits to support our diverse global team wherever they're based.

Specific benefits may vary by country and role.

title: AVP, DevOps Engineer
description:
Where Ambition Meets Innovation

Build a career that matches all your initiative with an impressive dose of innovation. From cutting-edge resources and a collaborative environment to the freedom to make an impact and more, you’ll find the ingredients you need at LPL Financial to shape your success while helping clients pursue their financial goals.


We are seeking an experienced AVP of DevOps Engineering to lead a team responsible for building and operating an AI-driven observability and reliability platform for enterprise-scale environments. This leader will oversee the organization's strategy for monitoring LPL environments using Dynatrace and similar OTEL, enable the development of intelligent automation and AI-powered operational capabilities, and drive adoption of modern reliability engineering practices across the enterprise.


The SRE lead will be responsible for analyzing logs, metrics, and traces, implementing dynamic alerting frameworks, and delivering self-healing capabilities that reduce MTTR, improve service resilience, and prevent outages. This role combines engineering leadership, SRE, platform engineering, observability, and applied AI/ML, with a strong focus on team development, operational excellence, automation, and business alignment.


The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of leading high-performing SRE, DevOps, or Platform Engineering teams in large-scale, mission-critical environments and driving reliability transformation initiatives across multiple business and technology organizations.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of Site Reliability Engineers focused on observability, reliability, automation, and operational excellence.
  • Define and execute the strategic roadmap for enterprise observability, AI-driven operations, and reliability engineering across the organization.
  • Establish and govern reliability standards, including SLOs, SLIs, error budgets, monitoring practices, and operational readiness requirements.
  • Drive adoption of enterprise observability solutions leveraging Dynatrace, including logs, metrics, traces, Real User Monitoring (RUM), and executive reporting dashboards.
  • Sponsor and oversee implementation of AI/ML-powered capabilities for predictive monitoring, anomaly detection, incident correlation, alert optimization, and root cause analysis.
  • Lead major incident management processes, post-incident reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce MTTR, incident recurrence, and operational toil.
  • Partner with application, infrastructure, cloud, security, and architecture teams to embed reliability, resilience, and operational best practices throughout the software lifecycle.
  • Champion self-healing and intelligent automation strategies, ensuring automated remediation capabilities are secure, auditable, scalable, and aligned with governance requirements.
  • Drive platform engineering and Infrastructure-as-Code adoption to improve system reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency across cloud and on-premises environments.
  • Establish metrics, KPIs, and operational governance frameworks to measure service health, team effectiveness, and reliability outcomes while communicating progress to senior leadership and stakeholders.

What are we looking for?

We’re looking for strong collaborators who deliver exceptional client experiences and thrive in fast-paced, team-oriented environments. Our ideal candidates pursue greatness, act with integrity, and are driven to help our clients succeed. We value those who embrace creativity, continuous improvement, and contribute to a culture where we win together and create and share joy in our work.


Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure Engineering, or Production Operations.
  • 3+ years of engineering leadership experience managing SRE, DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Operations teams.
  • 7+ years experience leading automation initiatives using programming and scripting languages such as Python, Go, Java, or similar technologies.
  • 2+ years experience of AI/ML-driven operational use cases, including anomaly detection, predictive monitoring, intelligent alerting, and incident correlation.
  • 7+ years experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), Kubernetes, container platforms, and modern CI/CD practices.

Core Competencies:

  • Site Reliability Engineering Expertise – Deep knowledge of SRE principles, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, availability, resiliency, and operational excellence.
  • Observability & Monitoring Leadership – Expertise in enterprise monitoring, Dynatrace, logging, metrics, tracing, AIOps, and service health management.
  • Incident & Crisis Management – Strong leadership during major incidents, root cause analysis, problem management, and continuous service improvement.
  • Automation & Platform Engineering – Ability to drive intelligent automation, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), CI/CD, and self-healing platform capabilities.
  • AI-Driven Operations (AIOps) – Understanding of AI/ML applications for anomaly detection, predictive monitoring, alert correlation, and operational intelligence.
  • Cloud & Distributed Systems Architecture – Strong knowledge of cloud platforms, Kubernetes, distributed systems, scalability, resilience, and reliability patterns.
  • Stakeholder Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration – Ability to influence and partner effectively with engineering, infrastructure, security, architecture, and business leaders.
  • Communication, Governance & Execution – Strong executive communication, decision-making, program leadership, operational governance, and results-driven execution skills.

$118,141.00 - $196,833.00


Actual base salary varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location. title: VP Product Management, Intelligent Data Layer
description:
Lead with Purpose, Unlock Your Team’s Passion

At LPL, people leaders hold the key to the employee experience — shaping culture, driving performance, and guiding individuals to new heights. Because when that happens, we all win – clients, LPL, and most importantly, our employees.


If you're ready to lead with intention and discover what’s possible, LPL Financial invites you to apply today.


Job Overview:

LPL is building the data foundation that enables AI across the firm. We are seeking a product leader to transform business information into reusable data products, shared business definitions, semantic models, and knowledge retrieval capabilities that support accurate and useful AI applications.


As Vice President, Product Management, Intelligent Data Layer, you will own the product strategy, roadmap, and lifecycle for this portfolio while leading a team of product managers and partnering with engineering, data science, AI application teams, and business stakeholders.


You will ground product development in defined business use cases by establishing an end-to-end path from source information through its use in an AI application. This “steel thread” approach will validate capabilities in production-oriented use cases and inform the development of reusable data, semantic, and retrieval products that can support additional applications across the firm.


Responsibilities:

  • Define and manage the Intelligent Data Layer product strategy, roadmap, priorities, and investment decisions, balancing business value, reuse, delivery effort, operating cost, and technical dependencies.
  • Lead the development and lifecycle management of reusable data products that make business facts, relationships, measures, and contextual information available to AI applications.
  • Establish semantic-layer capabilities that translate agreed business definitions into reusable data models, relationships, metrics, and calculations for consistent use across applications.
  • Lead knowledge and retrieval product capabilities, including enterprise search, knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and GraphRAG, and evaluate their performance against defined business questions and use cases.
  • Partner with AI application, engineering, data science, and business teams to deliver end-to-end use cases from source data through application consumption, using lessons from those implementations to expand reusable platform capabilities.
  • Own the product lifecycle from discovery and requirements through launch and ongoing improvement, defining product requirements for accuracy, data freshness, access permissions, source traceability, reliability, and support.
  • Establish product quality and AI evaluation measures for retrieval relevance, answer grounding, data accuracy, reliability, adoption, latency, and operating cost, and use results to prioritize product improvements.
  • Hire, develop, and lead product managers, establish delivery commitments with engineering leaders, and manage cross-functional dependencies and priorities.
  • Establish governance and ownership models with business and technology partners for shared definitions, semantic models, data products, and knowledge assets.
  • Measure adoption, product quality, reliability, and operating cost, and partner with application owners to evaluate business outcomes and inform roadmap investments.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for a product leader who will pursue greatness by establishing scalable data and knowledge capabilities that enable AI across the enterprise, act with integrity when making decisions involving data quality, access, governance, and investment, remain driven to help our clients succeed by connecting technology investments to meaningful business outcomes, win together by working across product, engineering, data science, AI, and business teams, and create and share joy by developing teams and building products that make it easier for others to deliver valuable solutions.


Requirements:

  • 10+ years of relevant product management experience, including experience with enterprise data products and production AI capabilities.
  • Experience leading product teams and delivering products across engineering, data science, and business organizations.
  • Experience taking data or retrieval products into production, supporting multiple consumers, and improving product performance following launch.
  • Working knowledge of semantic modeling, knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and AI evaluation methods.
  • Experience making product investment, build-versus-buy, and technical tradeoff decisions.

Preferences:

  • Ability to resolve competing business requirements and communicate product decisions to technical teams and senior leaders.
  • Financial services or other regulated-industry experience.

#LI-Hybrid


Pay Range:

$135,960.00 - $226,600.00


Actual base salary varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location. Additionally, LPL Total Rewards package is highly competitive, designed to support your success at work, at home, and at play – such as 401K matching, health benefits, employee stock options, paid time off, volunteer time off, and more. Your recruiter will be happy to discuss all that LPL has to offer!


Company Overview:

LPL Financial Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: LPLA) is among the fastest growing wealth management firms in the U.S. As a leader in the financial advisor-mediated marketplace(6) , LPL supports over 32,000 financial advisors and the wealth management practices of approximately 1,100 financial institutions, servicing and custodying approximately $2.3 trillion in brokerage and advisory assets on behalf of approximately 8 million Americans. The firm provides a wide range of advisor affiliation models, investment solutions, fintech tools and practice management services, ensuring that advisors and institutions have the flexibility to choose the business model, services, and technology resources they need to run thriving businesses. For further information about LPL, please visit www.lpl.com.


At LPL, independence means that advisors and institution leaders have the freedom they deserve to choose the business model, services, and technology resources that allow them to run a thriving business. They have the flexibility to do business their way. And they have the freedom to manage their client relationships, because they know their clients best. Simply put, we take care of our advisors and institutions, so they can take care of their clients.


For further information about LPL, please visit .


Join the LPL team and help us make a difference by turning life’s aspirations into financial realities. Please log in or create an account to apply to this position. Principals only. EOE.


Information on Interviews:

LPL will only communicate with a job applicant directly from an @lplfinancial.com email address and will never conduct an interview online or in a chatroom forum. During an interview, LPL will not request any form of payment from the applicant, or information regarding an applicant’s bank or credit card. Should you have any questions regarding the application process, please contact LPL’s Human Resources Solutions Center at (855) 575-6947.

title: Graduate Programme, Audit - Tunbridge Wells (Sept 2027)
description:
Why Start Your Career at S&W?

Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your successes and supports you to be yourself.

At S&W, you'll be given meaningful work from day one, while having the support, training and encouragement to help you succeed. You'll learn by doing, working alongside experienced colleagues, contributing to real projects and developing valuable professional skills from the start. As your confidence grows, so will your opportunities, with plenty of support along the way.

As one of the UK's fastest-growing accountancy and advisory firms, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career.

No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required. We're looking for people who are curious, motivated and ready to learn. What matters most is your attitude and desire to develop. We'll provide the training, support and opportunities to help you make the most of your potential.

The Audit & Assurance Team at S&W

Our Audit & Assurance team works with a diverse range of clients, from entrepreneurial and family-owned businesses to charities, not-for-profit organisations and larger established businesses across a variety of industries.

What sets Audit & Assurance at S&W apart is the breadth of experience you'll gain early in your career. You'll develop technical expertise, commercial awareness and a well-rounded understanding of how organisations operate, while working closely with experienced colleagues and gaining exposure to senior leaders and Partners. Together, this provides a strong foundation for a successful career in the profession.

Why Join our Tunbridge Wells office?

Our Tunbridge Wells office is easily accessible by car or via train, with the office being a 10–15 minute walk from Tunbridge Wells station. There are lots of surrounding green spaces and the office is also a short walk from the town. Our office is open plan with all departments working together on a fantastic mix of clients across a diverse range of industries. Our audit team is growing, and you'll be around plenty of other recent graduates and school leavers who have joined in recent years.

What Will You Be Doing?

As part of our Audit & Assurance team, you'll work alongside colleagues to deliver services to a variety of clients. You'll be involved in different stages of an engagement, gaining insight into how organisations operate and the role assurance plays in building confidence in financial reporting.

Alongside your role, you'll study towards the Associate Chartered Accountant (ACA) qualification, a prestigious qualification equivalent to a Level 7 Master's degree. Through a combination of professional training and practical experience, you'll build a strong foundation in audit, accountancy and wider business advisory services. You'll be supported with funded training, dedicated study time and guidance from colleagues who have successfully completed the qualification themselves.

Your work will include:

  • Analysing financial information
  • Testing processes and controls
  • Building relationships with client teams
  • Resolving audit and accountancy queries
  • Supporting a range of audit and accountancy projects

Whether you're based in one of our offices or working directly with clients, you'll contribute to meaningful work from day one while building the skills and confidence needed to become a trusted adviser.

To Be Successful in This Role

You'll be someone who:

  • Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges
  • Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships
  • Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems
  • Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution
  • Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals

You'll also need to:

  • Be committed to working towards the Associate Chartered Accountant (ACA) Level 7 professional qualification
  • Have obtained, or be predicted, a minimum 2:2 degree in any discipline
  • Have a minimum of 112 UCAS points from your top three A Levels (or equivalent), excluding General Studies
  • Have achieved a minimum Grade 5 (or equivalent) in GCSE English Language and Maths

No previous experience in accountancy, finance or professional services is required.

Your Learning & Development

We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning. You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team, helping you make the most of the opportunities available to you.

As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include

  • Fully funded training towards professional qualifications
  • Competitive salary
  • Private medical insurance
  • Life assurance
  • Pension contribution
  • Generous holiday package
  • Option to purchase additional holiday
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Season ticket loan
  • Eye care support
  • Shared parental leave

Our Commitment to Inclusion

We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment.

We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know.

IMPORTANT NOTES FOR COMPLETING YOUR APPLICATION

When you click on the 'I'm interested' button, you'll be taken to your profile page. We're currently updating it, but in the meantime:

  • We can only accept one application to any of our programmes in a recruitment season. If you're unsuccessful, you'll need to wait until the following recruitment season to reapply.
  • Under the Resume (CV) section, uploading a document is mandatory; however, it will not be formally reviewed.

title: Senior Software Engineer Full-Stack
description:
About Onit
We're redefining the future of legal operations through the power of AI. Our cutting-edge platform streamlines enterprise legal management, matter management, spend management and contract lifecycle processes, transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated solutions.

We’re a team of innovators using AI at the core to help legal departments become faster, smarter, and more strategic. As we continue to grow and expand the capabilities of our new AI-centric platform, we’re looking for bold thinkers and builders who are excited to shape the next chapter of legal tech.
If you're energized by meaningful work, love solving complex problems, and want to help modernize how legal teams operate, we’d love to meet you.

Position Summary

The Senior Software Engineer, Full-Stack builds substantial, interactive features inside Onit's enterprise legal operations platform, spanning enterprise legal management, matter management, spend management, and contract lifecycle management. Working across a Ruby on Rails backend and a modern JavaScript frontend, this individual contributor delivers data-dense, accurate, and resilient user experiences that fit seamlessly into the workflows legal teams rely on every day. The role partners closely with design, product, and the architecture team, owning features end to end from API to interface, with a strong focus on edge cases, performance, accessibility, and test coverage.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Build substantial, interactive features inside an existing enterprise product, without disrupting the workflows they sit within.
  • Implement data visualisations (line charts, comparison tables, range indicators) where the visual encoding carries real meaning and small inaccuracies mislead users.
  • Build filtering and comparison controls that update complex views in real time.
  • Implement every state the feature can be in: loading, error, empty, and the cases where there is insufficient data to show a comparison at all. These matter as much as the primary path.
  • Build and extend Ruby on Rails APIs, consume APIs built by the architecture team, and push back early when a contract does not serve the interface well.
  • Work closely with design, matching intent precisely and raising discrepancies rather than approximating.
  • Make sure features load asynchronously and never block or slow the workflows they are embedded in.
  • Build for accessibility and cross-browser consistency.
  • Instrument features so the team can measure how they are actually used.
  • Write tests that cover behaviour, including the degraded cases.

Required Skills:

  • 6+ years building production web applications, with significant frontend ownership and hands-on backend development.
  • Strong backend experience with Ruby on Rails: building and modifying APIs, data models, and services, not only consuming them.
  • Strong proficiency with a modern JavaScript framework (React, Angular, or Vue) and solid JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, including a real understanding of rendering and state management, not just framework APIs.
  • Experience building data-dense interfaces: charts, tables, dashboards, or comparison views where accuracy of presentation matters.
  • Experience working inside large existing codebases: reading unfamiliar code, following established conventions, and avoiding regressions.

    • Demonstrable care for edge cases, empty states, and error handling, backed by automated tests (e.g., RSpec and frontend testing frameworks).
    • Strong collaboration with designers and product managers; asks clarifying questions before building.
    • Working proficiency with AI coding tools (e.g., Claude, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate development, debugging, and test writing, with the judgment to review and validate AI-generated code before it ships.

title: Distribution Specialist
description:
At Memorial Hermann, we pursue a common goal of delivering high quality, efficient care while creating exceptional experiences for every member of our community. When we say every member of our community, that includes our employees. We know that when our employees feel cared for, heard and valued, they are inspired to create moments that exceed expectations, while prioritizing safety, compassion, personalization and efficiency. If you want to advance your career and contribute to our vision of creating healthier communities, now and for generations to come, we want you to be a part of our team.

Job Summary

The Distribution Specialist is responsible for accurately and timely fulfillment of customer’s orders from the Memorial Hermann Consolidated Service Center (CSC) to our acute care hospitals and other entities. The Specialist is responsible for several functions including: operating material handling equipment, radio frequency (RF) units, ring scanners, voice picking units and utilizing our warehouse management system (WMS) to pick orders. Automatous robots (AMRs) will be used throughout the CSC to pick orders from low unit of measure (LUM) areas. Position works with various departments within the CSC such as Customer Service, Logistics and Transportation to follow up and resolve customer order shipment issues. The Distribution Specialist typically reports to the Order Fulfillment Manager.

Job Description

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Education: High School diploma or GED preferred
Licenses/Certifications: Material Handling Equipment (MHE) certification preferred

Experience / Knowledge / Skills:

  • One (1) year of order fulfillment experience required

  • Prior experience successfully operating and maintaining forklifts, pallet jacks, reach trucks, and other electric material handling equipment

  • Excellent organizational and time management skills

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Accurately picks customer orders utilizing warehouse management system (WMS), robotics, and/or Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to complete multiple orders.

  • Sorts totes and cases of cardboard boxes or shipping containers by scanning, retrieving and placing orders on pallets.

  • Utilizes MHE to move all outbound customer orders to the shipping dock area.

  • Performs order induction activities for the low unit of measure (LUM) robotic picking activities.

  • Resolves any order errors prior to shipment.

  • Prepares, shrink wraps, and loads pallets onto delivery trucks for shipment.

  • May be required to work overtime and/or weekends.

  • Enforces and practices safety rules to maintain a safe working environment.

  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards by providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and colleagues.

  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Welding Instructor
description:
Job Overview


Western Welding Academy is on a mission to build a better generation of blue-collar craftsmen. We are forging the next generation of skilled welders through an unwavering commitment to work ethic, accountability, and integrity. By focusing on student outcomes, we provide industry-leading education and hands-on training in a real-world environment, preparing our students to meet and exceed the demands of the welding industry.

At Western Welding Academy, we believe wholeheartedly in our mission because we understand the fundamental role blue-collar tradespeople play in the fabric of America. This country was built on the backs of skilled workers—men and women who put in the hard labor that made our roads, bridges, buildings, and industries possible. Blue-collar men and women are the backbone of our economic system, vital to every sector from manufacturing to infrastructure. However, for too long, our nation has focused predominantly on white-collar jobs and the push to send every young person to college, leaving skilled trades underappreciated and underrepresented. Today, we are facing a monumental shift. A worldwide demographic collapse is causing industry and manufacturing to return to American soil, and yet, we lack the skilled labor force needed to meet the immense demand. Even before this shift, there was a substantial need for skilled tradespeople, but now, with global supply chains crumbling and reshoring becoming a necessity, the demand for welders and other skilled workers is skyrocketing. At Western Welding Academy, we see this as our mission, to equip the next generation with the skills they need to thrive, to build strong careers, and to restore the backbone of America's industrial strength. We are committed to filling this gap, one welder at a time, because we believe that the future of our country depends on the hands of those willing to build it.

Important Eligibility Requirement

Applicants must already be legally authorized to work in the United States. Western Welding Academy does not sponsor work visas or offer employment-based immigration support.

Why Join Western Welding Academy?

If you’re a seasoned welder with a passion for teaching, this is your chance to transform your experience into impact. As a Welding Instructor, you won’t just show students how to weld—you’ll shape the next generation of skilled tradespeople. You’ll be part of a team that values safety, professionalism, and craftsmanship, while working in a supportive environment where your expertise is respected and your growth is encouraged.

Here’s what’s in it for you: Your pay is only part of the picture. As a full-time team member, here's the real value of working at Western Welding Academy:

  • More Money. An additional $5,000 per year if you have your Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certificate.

  • Free medical option. Our Cigna HDHP is fully company-paid for you and your family. That's $0 out of your paycheck.

  • Money toward your health costs. Choose the HDHP and we add $1,000 a year to your Health Savings Account.

  • Company-paid life insurance. $75,000 in coverage at no cost to you.

  • 401(k) with a match. We match up to 3.5% of your pay to help you build for the future.

  • Dental and vision coverage through Principal at low monthly cost.

  • Generous PTO from your very first day.

  • Nine paid holidays, including Good Friday, Black Friday, and Christmas Eve.

  • A mission that matters. Your work helps put people into life-changing careers and helps rebuild America's skilled workforce, one welder at a time.

What You’ll Do

As a Welding Instructor, you’ll:

  • Lead by example with top-notch welding techniques, safety practices, and professionalism.

  • Deliver instruction in MIG, TIG, and stick welding, both in the classroom and shop.

  • Mentor students, track progress, and prepare them for industry certifications.

  • Foster safety, cleanliness, and accountability in the shop.

  • Stay sharp with ongoing training in welding processes and industry standards.

  • Help produce welders who can tackle any challenge with skill and confidence.

What We’re Looking For

  • 5–7 years of professional welding experience (pipe or structural).

  • Strong knowledge of welding processes, safety protocols, and industry standards.

  • Welding certifications (AWS preferred).

  • Experience training or mentoring others (instruction experience is a plus).

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and leadership skills.

  • Commitment to continuous learning and inspiring the next generation.

Physical Requirements

  • Able to stand, walk, and lift up to 50 lbs.

  • Willing to work 10-hour shifts, 5 days a week, with flexibility for overtime and occasional evenings/weekends.

  • Ability to travel between Western Welding Academy properties in Gillette, WY.

Join Our Mission

At Western Welding Academy, we’re not just teaching skills—we’re shaping futures. If you’re ready to make a lasting impact, keep your hands in the craft, and pass on your expertise to the welders of tomorrow, we’d love to have you on our team.

Apply today and help us build the future of welding.

title: Help Desk Engineering Manager
description:
mPower, Inc. is seeking an experienced and results-driven Help Desk Engineering Manager to lead and oversee the delivery of comprehensive IT support services for its customer.

The Help Desk Engineering Manager will provide strategic and operational leadership for a multidisciplinary team responsible for IT service delivery, Help Desk operations, desktop and systems support, asset management, and information security support. This position will lead a team of sourcing professionals and must have the ability to motivate others to meet the challenges of a face paced, collaborative, and results driven environment. NOTES

What We Offer

Diversity at Unilever is about inclusion, embracing differences, creating possibilities and growing together for better business performance. We embrace diversity in our workforce. This means giving full and fair consideration to all applicants and continuing development of all employees regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership, and pregnancy and maternity. We are also more than happy to provide reasonable adjustments during our application and interview process to enable you to be present your best self. To find out more, including about our Employee Resource Groups, please click here Equity, Diversity & Inclusion at Unilever | Unilever.


Recruitment Fraud

Cyber criminals advertise fake job adverts with prestigious employers as a way of stealing information or even defrauding individuals out of money. In the most sophisticated cases, they will set up fake websites, which have a similar address to companies like Unilever. They even conduct fake telephone interviews and then offer candidates a role with the proviso they pay a fee for background checks or to cover work visa costs. These types of attacks are becoming more common as more people are looking for employment in the economic climate.


How is Unilever tackling this?

Many of Unilever’s recruitment sites publish a warning to candidates about recruitment fraud. The Cyber Security team also proactively scan for signs of people setting up fake Unilever sites and act to close them down.


What can I do?

If you become aware of potential recruitment fraud, spot fake Unilever recruitment adverts or fake LinkedIn profiles, report them via Una Live Chat.


Unilever does not accept responsibility or liability for any candidates who are financially impacted by recruitment fraud. Your vigilance is key!

title: Educational Interpreter, Deaf and Hard of Hearing - Floater
description:
GRADE: G24 (Hourly Range/Step 1 - Step 9: $32.47 - $41.03)
MINIMUM HOURLY RATE: $32.47
STANDARD HOURS PER WEEK: 40
FTE: 1.0
MONTHS PER YEAR: 9
JOB CODE: 1201
POSITION TYPE: – PERMANENT/REGULAR
LOCATION: THORNTON, CO.

Adams 12 Five Star Schools is deeply committed to a community of excellence, equity, and inclusion in everything we do. We commit to eliminate the predictability of who is included in excellence and who is not. Adams 12 Five Star Schools puts students first and supports our district's mission to elevate student success for every student every day in every classroom. Candidates who can contribute to our goal are encouraged to apply and to identify their strengths in this area.

SUMMARY: Facilitate all communication, spoken and signed between Deaf/Hard of Hearing students and staff by using a manual mode of communication appropriate for the consumer. Tutor academic classes and lessons. Provide information to hearing staff and students to assist in better understanding the needs of Deaf/Hard of Hearing students.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Tasks Descriptions
1. Interpret and/or transliterate all academic instruction, films, assemblies, conferences, student meetings, individualized education plan meetings, field trips, extra-curricular activities and support services in and out of the classroom for Deaf/Hard of Hearing student(s). When voicing for Deaf/Hard of Hearing students(s), exhibit a good range of sophisticated vocabulary; native like expression, and infrequent use of circumlocution. Use clear articulation with consistent pronunciation, intonation, and affect to sound like native speaker. Have strong command of grammatical structure and evidence of command of complex instruction for complete comprehension. Speech is effortless and smooth; rate and production approach that of a native speaker comfortably.

Interpret: the process of changing spoken English into the preferred manual mode of communication for the Deaf/Hard of Hearing student, or vice versa.
Transliterate: the process of changing spoken English into a manual communication mode that maintains the grammar and syntax of the English language, or vice versa.
Translate: the process of interpreting the spoken English preferred manual mode of communication into spoken English, or vice versa.
2. Tutor Deaf/Hard of Hearing students (under the supervision of coordinating Teacher of the Deaf), both in and out of the classroom individually or in small groups by reinforcing concepts taught in the mainstream classes; assisting with missed assignments; modeling language; reinforcing vocabulary, study skills and life skills; assisting in learning variations of sign systems; developing of language concepts; changing CASE/PSE into written English; and teaching students the role of the interpreter, students' rights and responsibilities in how to use an interpreter.
3. As a member of the Deaf/Hard of Hearing student's education team, communicate with the team (e.g., mainstream teachers, teachers of the Deaf and support staff) to give and receive appropriate information/progress/problems that may impact a student's performance or learning, including, but not limited to, mode of communication, tutoring strategies, educational goals of student, curriculum content, classroom goals and student educational rights and services. May assist with personal hearing equipment (e.g. helping a student put hearing aids in) and/or assist with district hearing equipment (e.g. DM systems). May be asked to support instructors on monitoring behavior during class and extra-curricular activities; follow through with behavior programs established for individual students; use various equipment, augmentative communication systems or adaptations, any OT/PT requirements set forth in student I.E.P. (individual educational plan) and any medical conditions that require staff monitoring. Analyze and review instructional material to prepare for content and message delivery. Ensure appropriate logistics (e.g., lighting, seating, etc.). May be asked to assist Deaf Education Department staff by preparing instructional materials and various clerical duties as Interpreter time allows (e.g., scheduling interpreters for extra-curricular and after school activities, copying materials, and documenting information for DH/H Department, etc.).
4. Interpret and/or transliterate confidential in-school individual and group counseling/mental health sessions, disciplinary interactions, disciplinary hearings, and physical/occupational/speech therapy sessions between Deaf/Hard of Hearing student and staff. Interpret and/or transliterate for Deaf/Hard of Hearing students, or Deaf/Hard of Hearing staff at parent/teacher conferences, staff department meetings, district level meetings, in-services, and other required training. Interpret and/or transliterate for Deaf/hard of hearing parents of students in the District at parent/teacher conferences, back-to-school nights, after school performances, individual meetings and staff meetings. May provide Deaf awareness education to hearing staff and students through staff in-services, student groups and one-on-one communication. Promote positive public relations between the Deaf education program, the school and the community.
5. Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

EDUCATION AND RELATED WORK EXPERIENCE:
• Degree from an Interpreter Preparation Program (IPP) (Associates or Bachelors as required by IPP).
• Proficient in use of Conceptually Accurate Signed English (CASE)/Pidgin Signed English (PSE), and/or American Sign Language (ASL).
• No experience required; one (1) year of experience preferred in educational interpreting.

LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS, or CERTIFICATIONS:
• Criminal background check required for hire.
• Educational Interpreter Performance Assessment (EIPA) 3.5 or above.
• Must keep up-to-date any licenses, registrations, certifications, and/or authorizations required in this section.

APPLICATION INFORMATION:
All applicants (current district employees and external applicants) should list any and all work experience, including current district experience, when completing the employment application. Please include job titles and duties that you held while doing that job. Since the Human Resource department uses the application to screen for minimum qualifications required for each job, it is important to have a complete application so you will be considered for the position you are applying for.

SALARY INFORMATION:
All Classified positions are paid on an hourly basis. All Newly hired classified employees are placed initially on Step 1 of the pay grade for their position. Classified employees can advance an additional 7 steps (maximum Step 8) based on their previous experience. Final hourly placement on the Classified Salary schedule is dependent on the Grade Level for the position being posted and employees' previous work experience. "Grade" refers to position or job classification and "Step" refers to the number of work experience credit or service years. See our Classified Salary Schedule for hourly rates. For additional compensation information, please refer to The Classified Master Agreement.

BENEFITS INFORMATION:
Adams 12 Five Star Schools is committed to providing an environment that promotes a healthy employee population able to serve our students at the highest level. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision and life insurance as well as other programs for benefit eligible employees. The employee assistance program, voluntary life insurance through PERA, and 401(k), 403(b) & 457(b) plans are available to all employees regardless of hours worked and are available immediately (upon hire date).
To learn more about our benefits, please see our Benefits Overview.

THIS POSTING IS NOT INCLUSIVE OF THE JOB DESCRIPTION.

  • Supports HR processes including coaching and mentoring of staff.
  • Participates in appropriate role in disasters, fire drills, fires and other emergency situations and intervenes with clinical competence. Complies with and promotes safety and emergency procedures.
  • Exercises care in the operation and use of equipment and reference materials. Performs routine cleaning and preventative maintenance to ensure continued functioning of equipment. Maintain work areas in a clean, safe and organized manner.
  • Ensures safe care to patients, staff and visitors; adheres to all Memorial Hermann policies, procedures, and standards within budgetary specifications including time management, supply management, productivity and quality of service.
  • Promotes individual professional growth and development by meeting requirements for mandatory/continuing education and skills competency; supports department-based goals which contribute to the success of the organization; serves as preceptor, mentor and resource to less experienced staff.
  • Demonstrates commitment to caring for every member of our community by creating compassionate and personalized experiences. Models Memorial Hermann’s service standards by providing safe, caring, personalized and efficient experiences to patients and colleagues.
  • Other duties as assigned.

The Opportunity
Job classification: A5068 - Information Officer II

Hours per week: 36.25
Paid leave: 3 weeks vacation per year
Position End Date: January 6, 2028

This role provides administrative, logistical, and program coordination support for SAIT’s Study Abroad initiatives, including inbound and outbound student exchanges, Global Education Network (GEN) programs, international delegations, and Study Canada mobility opportunities. Working closely with students, faculty, partner institutions, and external stakeholders, the position ensures the successful planning, promotion, delivery, and evaluation of global learning experiences while supporting student safety, engagement, and program growth.

How you'll contribute
